recorded (outcome.json contract field)

Verbatim, as recorded with the run and sent to the agents.

- primitive to instantiate: `comb_mult_add_16` (precision INT16)
- computes: out = ax*ay + bx
- input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
- output ports: result[64]
- arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
- registers: none; the block is combinational, and `result` is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
- connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_mult_add_16 (precision INT16)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx
  • input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The design

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (channel width 300, median of five seeds, 1 to 5) has a worst register-to-register path of 11.6069 ns on its one clock tm3_clk_v0 (I/O pads not timed) and uses 224 DSP tiles (as packed at seed 1) of the device's 306. Its used logic-block area is 9.73358e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905) and its routed wirelength is 436921, so its area x delay x wirelength product, the objective, is 4.93619e+14. Its slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report) is in my_fir_f1: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report), in my_fir_f2 (endpoint group $dffe~642, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1, one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 11.293 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • The block's internal delay is fixed. Soft logic between a block's output and the next register adds to that stage; blocks in series each add their delay plus a wire.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.
Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_mult_add_16.v) are in sim_reference/.

PLAN:

What is converted and why

All 45 my_fir candidate products (7 modules x 6 instances of each = 270 products in the elaborated design) are converted. They are the design's critical arithmetic: path 1 (11.6069 ns, my_fir_f1) and path 2 (11.293 ns, my_fir_f2) are both one hard multiply followed by a six-deep ripple of 28-bit adders, and the other five my_fir modules are the same shape with five or six adder levels. Converting one module alone would stop at 11.293 ns, so all seven are converted together; only then does the whole my_fir family drop to ~9.1 ns.

A straight T1 rewrite (one block per product as written) is not possible: 270 blocks, each taking a DSP tile alone, plus the tiles the unchanged fltr_compute 9x9 products need, is ~354 tiles against a 306-tile device, and it would roughly double DSP area. The rewrite is therefore T2: every one of these filters has a symmetric coefficient set (my_fir_f1 29,101,15,235,15,101,29 at lines 1440-1449; f2/h2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4 at 1500-1506 and 1675-1681; f3 12,77,148,-,148,77,12 at 1561-1567; h1 15,25,193,-,193,25,15 at 1616-1625; h3/h4 9,56,109,-,109,56,9 at 1734-1740 and 1792-1798), so the taps are pre-added in pairs and each pair multiplied once: 45 products per instance set become 24. Same value computed, fewer multiplies.

What is left and why

All 46 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 lines 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071; 276 products elaborated) are left, for one shared reason with two parts. (a) Cost: they are 8-bit-by-constant multiplies that the baseline packs four to a DSP tile; on this block each one takes a tile alone. Even folded by symmetry they would need 25 blocks per v_fltr instance, 150 tiles, which on top of the 144 my_fir blocks is 294 of 306 tiles and roughly +66 tiles (+1.7e7 area, ~+17%) against the packing they get now. (b) No benefit: the row says their products are registered one stage before the sum (q1..q7, e.g. lines 859-865 then 867), so their multiply stage is ~3 ns and their sum stage is a six-level adder chain at about 0.060 + 0.960 + 6x1.069 + 0.6 = 8.0 ns, below the 9.1 ns the my_fir stages keep. No block placed there can shorten the critical path, and the tiles it costs would raise area and wirelength. They stay exactly as they are.

Blocks, tiles

144 blocks (24 instantiation statements across the 7 my_fir module bodies, 6 instances each). The design then uses about 230 DSP tiles of 306: the 144 block tiles plus roughly 86 tiles for the 276 unchanged 9x9 fltr_compute products (the 57 tiles that already hold only those, plus about 29 more for the ones that currently share tiles with the my_fir 18x19 multiplies). That is +6 tiles against the baseline 224, i.e. about +1.5e6 of 9.73e7 area, and it is an upper estimate: the baseline packs the 270 my_fir products one or two to a tile, so if many sat one to a tile the count lands nearer 205 and DSP area falls. Either way the device is not full (76 tiles of headroom) and no block is forced to share.

Longest series of blocks, and the stage it sits in

The longest series of blocks in any stage is one block, 2.14 ns. No block feeds another block's bx: all four (or three) folded products in a module become available at the same instant, so chaining two blocks would cost 2.14 + 1.17 = 3.31 ns on the path where a soft adder level costs 1.069 ns, and a two-deep block chain would put the stage back at about 11.2 ns, i.e. no better than the 11.6069 ns baseline. bx is therefore tied to 32'd0 on every block and the three or four block results are combined in a two-level soft adder tree. The resulting stage, which is still the slowest in the design, is:

0.060 (flip-flop clock to output) + 0.960 (wire into the soft pre-adder) + 1.069 (16-bit pre-adder level) + 1.170 (wire into the block) + 2.140 (block) + 0.960 (wire, block into soft logic) + 2 x 1.069 (two adder levels of the output tree) + ~0.6 (final cell and wire into the enabled flip-flop) = 9.1 ns,

against 11.6069 ns for the baseline slowest stage and 11.293 ns for the second. All 42 elaborated my_fir stages land at this figure (the three-product modules are the same depth as the four-product ones), so unlike a single-module rewrite this one is not capped by path 2. The same model reproduces the baseline path: 0.060 + 1.419 + 2.140 + 0.960 + 6 x 1.069 + ~0.6 = 11.6 ns.

Soft logic moving out of which stage

Out of each my_fir dout stage (the slowest stage, 42 instances of it) go the five or six chained 28-bit adders and the LUT that ended the baseline path. Into the same stage go three 16-bit pre-adders (one level, in parallel) and a two-level tree of 28-bit adders, and for my_fir_f3 one extra 28-bit adder plus eight LUTs of carry correction. Net per instance: six soft adder levels become three, and three of the remaining adders shrink from 28 bits to 16. That is the whole of the 2.5 ns the stage loses, and it also takes roughly 25 logic cells per instance (about 1000 cells, ~100 clusters, ~2.5e6 area) out of the cluster count, which offsets the ~+1.5e6 of extra DSP tiles; expect area to come out at or just below baseline. Wirelength should be flat to slightly lower: 144 block tiles replace ~140-167 multiplier tiles, and 42 copies of a six-deep 28-bit carry-chain cascade become two-deep trees. With delay at 9.1/11.6069 = 0.78 of baseline, the objective should land near 3.8e14 against 4.93619e14.

Register stages, before and after

For every one of the 45 converted regions the count is unchanged: 0 register stages between the operands and the product, and 0 between the product and the sum. Before, din and n_delay_reg1..6 (registered at lines 1478-1483 and the matching lines in the other six modules) feed the multiply and the adder chain combinationally, and the result is captured by the enabled dout flip-flop in the same cycle. After, the same registers feed the pre-adder, the block (which is combinational, result valid in the cycle the inputs are applied) and the output tree, and the same enabled dout flip-flop captures the result in the same cycle. The rewrite adds no register, moves no register, and relies on no power-up value; the n_delay_reg shift, the output_data_ready logic and the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) enable are untouched, so behaviour after any reset is identical.

Why the folded form computes the same value

Each block reads ax, ay, bx unsigned and returns the exact 64-bit ax*ay+bx; all taps and coefficients here are unsigned (din is [15:0] at line 1460 and the COEF defines at lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798 are all positive literals, the commented-out negative forms are not used). For the six modules other than f3 the pre-added pair fits in 16 bits (see the bound below), so (x+y)*C = x*C + y*C exactly and no block operand or result is truncated: the largest single product is 42902 x 101 = 4.33e6 and the largest module total is 1.26e7, both far inside 2^28, so taking result[27:0] and summing at 28 bits reproduces the original 32-bit expression truncated to the 28-bit dout.

For my_fir_f3 no bound is needed: two 16-bit values always fit in 17 bits, so s06, s15, s24 are exact, and 12*s06 = 12*s06[15:0] + 12*65536*s06[16]. The three carry-outs are collected into corr = 12*s06[16] + 77*s15[16] + 148*s24[16] (at most 237, a three-input function, eight LUTs) and corr << 16 is added as a fourth term of the output tree rather than through a bx port, so it rides in parallel with the blocks and adds nothing to the stage. f3's total is at most 474 x 35891 = 1.70e7, inside 2^28.

ASSUMES: every din reaching a my_fir module is at most 21451, so a pre-added tap pair is at most 42902 and fits in the 16-bit ax port. This is forced by the design, not by the stimulus: each my_fir_* din is an h_fltr port driven straight from a v_fltr output (lines 185-197, 514-520), which is fltr_compute_*.dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] (lines 868, 898, 937, 968, 1001, 1039, 1074); d_out_tmp is the exact 20-bit sum of seven non-negative 17-bit products of an 8-bit fifo tap (lines 689-704, 714, and the q1..q7 assignments at 859-865, 889-895, 959-965, 992-998, 1030-1036, 1065-1071), and the 8-bit width is fixed by the top-level ports v_d_reg_s1/s2/s4_left/right_2to0 (lines 49-57). The coefficient sums give dout bounds of 18200 (f1), 21451 (f2 and h2), 14981 (h1), 15427 (h3), 19061 (h4); with the port pairing at lines 514-520 the worst case any folded module sees is 21451 (my_fir_f1 and my_fir_h1, from fltr_compute_f2 and fltr_compute_h2), i.e. 42902 against the 65535 the port holds. fltr_compute_f3 is the one that can exceed 32767 (bound 35891, coefficient sum 1126 at lines 928-934), and that is exactly the module feeding my_fir_f3, which is why my_fir_f3 carries the carry correction and depends on no bound at all.

DESIGN_CHANGE: fltr_compute_f3 is the only vertical filter whose dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] can exceed 15 bits (coefficient sum 1126 at lines 928-934 against 673 or less everywhere else). If its output shift were widened by one bit, or its coefficients scaled like the other six, my_fir_f3 could fold with plain 16-bit pre-adders like the rest and would drop the three 17-bit adders, the eight correction LUTs and one 28-bit adder per instance (6 instances).

1	// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
6	// reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_mult_add_16 (
8	    input  [15:0] ax,
9	    input  [15:0] ay,
10	    input  [31:0] bx,
11	    output [63:0] result
12	);
13	
14	    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
15	    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact
16	
17	    assign result = sum;
18	
19	endmodule

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_mult_add_16 (precision INT16)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx
  • input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

    bx is 32'd0 on all 144 blocks. All 24 block instantiations live in the 7 module bodies, so the 6 instances of each module give 144 blocks in the elaborated design.

PLAN:

What is converted and why

All 45 my_fir candidate products (7 modules x 6 instances of each = 270 products in the elaborated design) are converted. They are the design's critical arithmetic: path 1 (11.6069 ns, my_fir_f1) and path 2 (11.293 ns, my_fir_f2) are both one hard multiply followed by a six-deep ripple of 28-bit adders, and the other five my_fir modules are the same shape with five or six adder levels. Converting one module alone would stop at 11.293 ns, so all seven are converted together; only then does the whole my_fir family drop to ~9.1 ns.

A straight T1 rewrite (one block per product as written) is not possible: 270 blocks, each taking a DSP tile alone, plus the tiles the unchanged fltr_compute 9x9 products need, is ~354 tiles against a 306-tile device, and it would roughly double DSP area. The rewrite is therefore T2: every one of these filters has a symmetric coefficient set (my_fir_f1 29,101,15,235,15,101,29 at lines 1440-1449; f2/h2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4 at 1500-1506 and 1675-1681; f3 12,77,148,-,148,77,12 at 1561-1567; h1 15,25,193,-,193,25,15 at 1616-1625; h3/h4 9,56,109,-,109,56,9 at 1734-1740 and 1792-1798), so the taps are pre-added in pairs and each pair multiplied once: 45 products per instance set become 24. Same value computed, fewer multiplies.

What is left and why

All 46 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 lines 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071; 276 products elaborated) are left, for one shared reason with two parts. (a) Cost: they are 8-bit-by-constant multiplies that the baseline packs four to a DSP tile; on this block each one takes a tile alone. Even folded by symmetry they would need 25 blocks per v_fltr instance, 150 tiles, which on top of the 144 my_fir blocks is 294 of 306 tiles and roughly +66 tiles (+1.7e7 area, ~+17%) against the packing they get now. (b) No benefit: the row says their products are registered one stage before the sum (q1..q7, e.g. lines 859-865 then 867), so their multiply stage is ~3 ns and their sum stage is a six-level adder chain at about 0.060 + 0.960 + 6x1.069 + 0.6 = 8.0 ns, below the 9.1 ns the my_fir stages keep. No block placed there can shorten the critical path, and the tiles it costs would raise area and wirelength. They stay exactly as they are.

Blocks, tiles

144 blocks (24 instantiation statements across the 7 my_fir module bodies, 6 instances each). The design then uses about 230 DSP tiles of 306: the 144 block tiles plus roughly 86 tiles for the 276 unchanged 9x9 fltr_compute products (the 57 tiles that already hold only those, plus about 29 more for the ones that currently share tiles with the my_fir 18x19 multiplies). That is +6 tiles against the baseline 224, i.e. about +1.5e6 of 9.73e7 area, and it is an upper estimate: the baseline packs the 270 my_fir products one or two to a tile, so if many sat one to a tile the count lands nearer 205 and DSP area falls. Either way the device is not full (76 tiles of headroom) and no block is forced to share.

Longest series of blocks, and the stage it sits in

The longest series of blocks in any stage is one block, 2.14 ns. No block feeds another block's bx: all four (or three) folded products in a module become available at the same instant, so chaining two blocks would cost 2.14 + 1.17 = 3.31 ns on the path where a soft adder level costs 1.069 ns, and a two-deep block chain would put the stage back at about 11.2 ns, i.e. no better than the 11.6069 ns baseline. bx is therefore tied to 32'd0 on every block and the three or four block results are combined in a two-level soft adder tree. The resulting stage, which is still the slowest in the design, is:

0.060 (flip-flop clock to output) + 0.960 (wire into the soft pre-adder) + 1.069 (16-bit pre-adder level) + 1.170 (wire into the block) + 2.140 (block) + 0.960 (wire, block into soft logic) + 2 x 1.069 (two adder levels of the output tree) + ~0.6 (final cell and wire into the enabled flip-flop) = 9.1 ns,

against 11.6069 ns for the baseline slowest stage and 11.293 ns for the second. All 42 elaborated my_fir stages land at this figure (the three-product modules are the same depth as the four-product ones), so unlike a single-module rewrite this one is not capped by path 2. The same model reproduces the baseline path: 0.060 + 1.419 + 2.140 + 0.960 + 6 x 1.069 + ~0.6 = 11.6 ns.

Soft logic moving out of which stage

Out of each my_fir dout stage (the slowest stage, 42 instances of it) go the five or six chained 28-bit adders and the LUT that ended the baseline path. Into the same stage go three 16-bit pre-adders (one level, in parallel) and a two-level tree of 28-bit adders, and for my_fir_f3 one extra 28-bit adder plus eight LUTs of carry correction. Net per instance: six soft adder levels become three, and three of the remaining adders shrink from 28 bits to 16. That is the whole of the 2.5 ns the stage loses, and it also takes roughly 25 logic cells per instance (about 1000 cells, ~100 clusters, ~2.5e6 area) out of the cluster count, which offsets the ~+1.5e6 of extra DSP tiles; expect area to come out at or just below baseline. Wirelength should be flat to slightly lower: 144 block tiles replace ~140-167 multiplier tiles, and 42 copies of a six-deep 28-bit carry-chain cascade become two-deep trees. With delay at 9.1/11.6069 = 0.78 of baseline, the objective should land near 3.8e14 against 4.93619e14.

Register stages, before and after

For every one of the 45 converted regions the count is unchanged: 0 register stages between the operands and the product, and 0 between the product and the sum. Before, din and n_delay_reg1..6 (registered at lines 1478-1483 and the matching lines in the other six modules) feed the multiply and the adder chain combinationally, and the result is captured by the enabled dout flip-flop in the same cycle. After, the same registers feed the pre-adder, the block (which is combinational, result valid in the cycle the inputs are applied) and the output tree, and the same enabled dout flip-flop captures the result in the same cycle. The rewrite adds no register, moves no register, and relies on no power-up value; the n_delay_reg shift, the output_data_ready logic and the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) enable are untouched, so behaviour after any reset is identical.

Why the folded form computes the same value

Each block reads ax, ay, bx unsigned and returns the exact 64-bit ax*ay+bx; all taps and coefficients here are unsigned (din is [15:0] at line 1460 and the COEF defines at lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798 are all positive literals, the commented-out negative forms are not used). For the six modules other than f3 the pre-added pair fits in 16 bits (see the bound below), so (x+y)*C = x*C + y*C exactly and no block operand or result is truncated: the largest single product is 42902 x 101 = 4.33e6 and the largest module total is 1.26e7, both far inside 2^28, so taking result[27:0] and summing at 28 bits reproduces the original 32-bit expression truncated to the 28-bit dout.

For my_fir_f3 no bound is needed: two 16-bit values always fit in 17 bits, so s06, s15, s24 are exact, and 12*s06 = 12*s06[15:0] + 12*65536*s06[16]. The three carry-outs are collected into corr = 12*s06[16] + 77*s15[16] + 148*s24[16] (at most 237, a three-input function, eight LUTs) and corr << 16 is added as a fourth term of the output tree rather than through a bx port, so it rides in parallel with the blocks and adds nothing to the stage. f3's total is at most 474 x 35891 = 1.70e7, inside 2^28.

ASSUMES: every din reaching a my_fir module is at most 21451, so a pre-added tap pair is at most 42902 and fits in the 16-bit ax port. This is forced by the design, not by the stimulus: each my_fir_* din is an h_fltr port driven straight from a v_fltr output (lines 185-197, 514-520), which is fltr_compute_*.dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] (lines 868, 898, 937, 968, 1001, 1039, 1074); d_out_tmp is the exact 20-bit sum of seven non-negative 17-bit products of an 8-bit fifo tap (lines 689-704, 714, and the q1..q7 assignments at 859-865, 889-895, 959-965, 992-998, 1030-1036, 1065-1071), and the 8-bit width is fixed by the top-level ports v_d_reg_s1/s2/s4_left/right_2to0 (lines 49-57). The coefficient sums give dout bounds of 18200 (f1), 21451 (f2 and h2), 14981 (h1), 15427 (h3), 19061 (h4); with the port pairing at lines 514-520 the worst case any folded module sees is 21451 (my_fir_f1 and my_fir_h1, from fltr_compute_f2 and fltr_compute_h2), i.e. 42902 against the 65535 the port holds. fltr_compute_f3 is the one that can exceed 32767 (bound 35891, coefficient sum 1126 at lines 928-934), and that is exactly the module feeding my_fir_f3, which is why my_fir_f3 carries the carry correction and depends on no bound at all.

DESIGN_CHANGE: fltr_compute_f3 is the only vertical filter whose dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] can exceed 15 bits (coefficient sum 1126 at lines 928-934 against 673 or less everywhere else). If its output shift were widened by one bit, or its coefficients scaled like the other six, my_fir_f3 could fold with plain 16-bit pre-adders like the rest and would drop the three 17-bit adders, the eight correction LUTs and one 28-bit adder per instance (6 instances).

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_mult_add_16.v) are in sim_reference/.

REVISE

1. Assumptions — the ASSUMES: line is false as written, and the mapping that rests on it violates Same behavior.

The ASSUMES says "d_out_tmp is the exact 20-bit sum of seven non-negative 17-bit products". It is not. At stereovision2.v:867 (and the identical lines 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073) each 17-bit q is sign-extended: {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}. Where a partial product reaches 2^16 the term is subtracted rather than added, d_out_tmp wraps mod 2^20, and dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] can be anything up to 65535 — not the coefficient-sum bound the plan computes.

Two of the seven vertical filters have a partial product that reaches 2^16:

  • fltr_compute_f1, line 862: q4 <= din[31:24] * 9'b100010101 (277); 255×277 = 70635 ≥ 2^16. With buff_out4=255 and the other taps 0 (din packing at line 706), d_out_tmp = 20'hF13EB = 988139 and dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] = 57981, not ≤ 18200.
  • fltr_compute_h4, line 1068: q4 <= din[31:24] * 9'b101000100 (324); 255×324 = 82620 ≥ 2^16. Same stimulus gives d_out_tmp = 1000124 and dout = 59479, not ≤ 19061.

By the pairing at lines 514–520, fltr_compute_f1.dout drives my_fir_f2.din (line 515, port vidin_in_f1) and fltr_compute_h4.dout drives my_fir_h3.din (line 519, port vidin_in_h4). The plan gives those two modules the plain folded form with a 16-bit pre-adder and no carry correction, so when din + n_delay_reg6 ≥ 65536 the ax port truncates and dout is wrong by 65536×COEF0 — 262144 for my_fir_f2 (line 1542, coef 4) and 589824 for my_fir_h3 (line 1775, coef 9). The same holds for the (n1+n5) and (n2+n4) pairs. These errors reach compared outputs: vidin_out_reg_f2/_h3 (lines 531, 547) feed steer_fltr (521), re_p_tmp_3/im_p_tmp_3 (633, 636), re_p/re_n/im_p/im_n (640–643, 646–649), and port_bus_2to1 (199). The top-level inputs v_d_reg_s*_2to0 are unconstrained 8-bit ports (lines 49–57, registered at 433 and passed through fifo496, 698–704, 1124–1132), so 237–255 at the centre tap is reachable and the testbench drives those ports full-width random.

The ASSUMES bound does hold for the other four: all partial products of fltr_compute_f2 (889–895), h2 (992–998), h1 (959–965) and h3 (1030–1036) are < 2^16 (max 255×255 = 65025, 255×193 = 49215, 255×147 = 37485), so the sign extension is a no-op there and the bounds 21451 / 21451 / 14981 / 15427 are correct for my_fir_f1, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h2, my_fir_h4 respectively (pairs ≤ 42902 < 65536). my_fir_f3 needs no bound, as the plan says — its 17-bit sums and corr = 12*s06[16] + 77*s15[16] + 148*s24[16] are correct for any 16-bit din.

What to change: give my_fir_f2 (1542–1548) and my_fir_h3 (1775–1780) the same 17-bit pre-add plus carry correction used for my_fir_f3 — corr = 4*s06[16] + 42*s15[16] + 163*s24[16] (≤ 209) for f2, corr = 9*s06[16] + 56*s15[16] + 109*s24[16] (≤ 174) for h3, added as {4'b0,corr,16'b0} in the 28-bit output tree (totals stay inside 2^28: 673×65535 = 4.41e7, 348×65535 = 2.28e7). Then restate ASSUMES: to cover only my_fir_f1, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h2, my_fir_h4, justified by "every partial product in fltr_compute_f2/h2/h1/h3 is below 2^16, so the sign extension at lines 897/1000/967/1038 is a no-op", citing lines 889–898, 959–968, 992–1001, 1030–1039 and 514–520 — not the "non-negative products" argument, which is wrong.

2. Assumptions / design claim — the DESIGN_CHANGE statement is factually wrong.

"fltr_compute_f3 is the only vertical filter whose dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] can exceed 15 bits" is false for the same reason: fltr_compute_f1 (862, 867) and fltr_compute_h4 (1068, 1073) also exceed 15 bits through the wrap shown above. Restate or drop it.

3. Consequential updates once the correction is added.

The stage figure and the soft-logic statement describe only my_fir_f3 as carrying the extra 28-bit adder and correction LUTs; with f2 and h3 corrected, the "what leaves which stage" paragraph and the per-instance adder/LUT accounting must name f1→f2's and h4→h3's paths too (three modules with correction, not one). The block count stays 144 and the register-stage statement (0 before and 0 after, operands din/n_delay_reg1..6 at 1478–1483 and the matching lines, enabled dout flip-flop under new_data_rdy, line 1476) is correct and unaffected.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • The block's internal delay is fixed. Soft logic between a block's output and the next register adds to that stage; blocks in series each add their delay plus a wire.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.
The plan reviewer's reply to your previous plan

I'll read the design source now.

REVISE

1. Assumptions — the ASSUMES: line is false as written, and the mapping that rests on it violates Same behavior.

The ASSUMES says "d_out_tmp is the exact 20-bit sum of seven non-negative 17-bit products". It is not. At stereovision2.v:867 (and the identical lines 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073) each 17-bit q is sign-extended: {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}. Where a partial product reaches 2^16 the term is subtracted rather than added, d_out_tmp wraps mod 2^20, and dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] can be anything up to 65535 — not the coefficient-sum bound the plan computes.

Two of the seven vertical filters have a partial product that reaches 2^16:

  • fltr_compute_f1, line 862: q4 <= din[31:24] * 9'b100010101 (277); 255×277 = 70635 ≥ 2^16. With buff_out4=255 and the other taps 0 (din packing at line 706), d_out_tmp = 20'hF13EB = 988139 and dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] = 57981, not ≤ 18200.
  • fltr_compute_h4, line 1068: q4 <= din[31:24] * 9'b101000100 (324); 255×324 = 82620 ≥ 2^16. Same stimulus gives d_out_tmp = 1000124 and dout = 59479, not ≤ 19061.

By the pairing at lines 514–520, fltr_compute_f1.dout drives my_fir_f2.din (line 515, port vidin_in_f1) and fltr_compute_h4.dout drives my_fir_h3.din (line 519, port vidin_in_h4). The plan gives those two modules the plain folded form with a 16-bit pre-adder and no carry correction, so when din + n_delay_reg6 ≥ 65536 the ax port truncates and dout is wrong by 65536×COEF0 — 262144 for my_fir_f2 (line 1542, coef 4) and 589824 for my_fir_h3 (line 1775, coef 9). The same holds for the (n1+n5) and (n2+n4) pairs. These errors reach compared outputs: vidin_out_reg_f2/_h3 (lines 531, 547) feed steer_fltr (521), re_p_tmp_3/im_p_tmp_3 (633, 636), re_p/re_n/im_p/im_n (640–643, 646–649), and port_bus_2to1 (199). The top-level inputs v_d_reg_s*_2to0 are unconstrained 8-bit ports (lines 49–57, registered at 433 and passed through fifo496, 698–704, 1124–1132), so 237–255 at the centre tap is reachable and the testbench drives those ports full-width random.

The ASSUMES bound does hold for the other four: all partial products of fltr_compute_f2 (889–895), h2 (992–998), h1 (959–965) and h3 (1030–1036) are < 2^16 (max 255×255 = 65025, 255×193 = 49215, 255×147 = 37485), so the sign extension is a no-op there and the bounds 21451 / 21451 / 14981 / 15427 are correct for my_fir_f1, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h2, my_fir_h4 respectively (pairs ≤ 42902 < 65536). my_fir_f3 needs no bound, as the plan says — its 17-bit sums and corr = 12*s06[16] + 77*s15[16] + 148*s24[16] are correct for any 16-bit din.

What to change: give my_fir_f2 (1542–1548) and my_fir_h3 (1775–1780) the same 17-bit pre-add plus carry correction used for my_fir_f3 — corr = 4*s06[16] + 42*s15[16] + 163*s24[16] (≤ 209) for f2, corr = 9*s06[16] + 56*s15[16] + 109*s24[16] (≤ 174) for h3, added as {4'b0,corr,16'b0} in the 28-bit output tree (totals stay inside 2^28: 673×65535 = 4.41e7, 348×65535 = 2.28e7). Then restate ASSUMES: to cover only my_fir_f1, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h2, my_fir_h4, justified by "every partial product in fltr_compute_f2/h2/h1/h3 is below 2^16, so the sign extension at lines 897/1000/967/1038 is a no-op", citing lines 889–898, 959–968, 992–1001, 1030–1039 and 514–520 — not the "non-negative products" argument, which is wrong.

2. Assumptions / design claim — the DESIGN_CHANGE statement is factually wrong.

"fltr_compute_f3 is the only vertical filter whose dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] can exceed 15 bits" is false for the same reason: fltr_compute_f1 (862, 867) and fltr_compute_h4 (1068, 1073) also exceed 15 bits through the wrap shown above. Restate or drop it.

3. Consequential updates once the correction is added.

The stage figure and the soft-logic statement describe only my_fir_f3 as carrying the extra 28-bit adder and correction LUTs; with f2 and h3 corrected, the "what leaves which stage" paragraph and the per-instance adder/LUT accounting must name f1→f2's and h4→h3's paths too (three modules with correction, not one). The block count stays 144 and the register-stage statement (0 before and 0 after, operands din/n_delay_reg1..6 at 1478–1483 and the matching lines, enabled dout flip-flop under new_data_rdy, line 1476) is correct and unaffected.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_mult_add_16.v) are in sim_reference/.

PLAN:

What is converted. All 45 candidate ids in the seven my_fir_* modules (lines 1486-1492, 1542-1548, 1602-1607, 1661-1666, 1716-1722, 1775-1780, 1833-1838). Each module's seven (or six) products are regrouped by the symmetry of its coefficients — C0=C6, C1=C5, C2=C4 in every one of the seven, verified against the `define blocks at 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798 — into three folded products plus, in f1/f2/h2, the centre tap. This is T2: the products are regrouped, no register is moved or added.

What is left, and why. All 46 fltr_compute_* ids (lines 859-865, 889-895, 928-934, 959-965, 992-998, 1030-1036, 1065-1071) are left, for three reasons that apply to every one of them:

  1. Tile cost. These are 8x9 constant products packed four to a DSP tile; a comb_mult_add_16 takes a tile alone. Even folded by symmetry (these coefficient sets are symmetric too) they would need 25 blocks per v_fltr instance, 150 blocks, 150 extra tiles. With the 144 blocks of this plan the design would need more than the device's 306 tiles, and the added DSP area (150 x 253779 = 3.8e7) far exceeds the ~20-bit soft adder trees it would remove.
  2. Register position. The table's "products registered 1 stage before the sum" matches lines 859-867: q1..q7 are registered, the sum is in the next stage. A combinational mult-add can only absorb that sum by retiming a register across the 56-bit din port (56 added flip-flops per instance), which is outside what the rewrite needs.
  3. Signedness. The sum at 867/897/936/967/1000/1038/1073 sign-extends each 17-bit q ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}) and wraps mod 2^20. The block is unsigned, so each term whose q[16] can be 1 — which happens in fltr_compute_f1 (line 862, coefficient 277: 255*277 = 70635) and fltr_compute_h4 (line 1068, coefficient 324: 255*324 = 82620) — would need an explicit -2^17 correction term per product on top of everything else.

Blocks and tiles. 4 blocks in each of my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2 and 3 blocks in each of my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4 = 24 per h_fltr instance, x6 instances = 144 blocks. They replace all 270 two_mult_18x19 multiplies of the my_fir modules (45 per h_fltr x 6), which at two to a tile occupy about 135 tiles; 224 - 135 + 144 = 233 tiles, inside the 306 the device has. The 57 tiles holding the 9x9 fltr_compute products are untouched. Net DSP area +9 x 253779 = +2.3e6 (+2.3%); the soft logic removed is larger (below), so total logic-block area falls.

Longest series of blocks, and the stage. Two blocks, never more: mul_a->mul_b, and mul_c->mul_d (7-tap) or mul_c alone (6-tap), the two chains joined by one 28-bit soft adder. Worst stage, 7-tap with the correction (my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2): flip-flop 0.060 + pre-adder level 1.069 + correction LUT 1.069 + wire into block 1.419 + block 2.14 + block-to-block wire 1.17 + block 2.14 + wire into soft logic 0.960 + final 28-bit adder level 1.069 = 11.10 ns, against the baseline slowest stage 11.6069 ns. The same stage without the correction LUT on it (the s24 data path, and the whole of the four 6-tap modules) is 10.03 ns; the correction path in a 6-tap module is 7.79 ns, since mul_c there feeds the final adder directly. Both baseline paths 1 and 2 are my_fir stages of the identical shape (one DSP multiply, six adder levels, one LUT, enabled flip-flop) and all 42 my_fir instances share that shape, so every stage between 11.293 and 11.6069 ns is rewritten; the period after the rewrite is set either by this 11.10 ns stage or by an untouched stage at or below 11.293 ns.

Soft logic that leaves, and from which stage. Out of each my_fir stage (the stage that holds baseline paths 1 and 2, the slowest and second slowest): the 6-deep 28-bit adder chain (5-deep in the 6-tap modules), i.e. about 168 adder cells per 7-tap instance and 140 per 6-tap instance. Into it: three 16-bit pre-adders (48 cells), one 28-bit final adder (28 cells) and the correction LUTs (about 8). Net about 84 cells saved per 7-tap instance and 56 per 6-tap, 476 per h_fltr instance, about 2900 cells over the six instances — on the order of 290 clusters, 8e6 area units, roughly 8% of the 9.73e7 baseline, against the +2.3e6 of DSP. Fewer 28-bit nets in the adder trees should also shorten routed wirelength. No other stage gains logic: the pre-adders and the correction LUT sit in the same stage the adder tree left.

Register stages, before and after. For every converted region, before: the operands din and n_delay_reg1..6 (lines 1467-1472, 1478-1483 and the matching lines in each module) are flip-flop outputs, the product and the whole sum are combinational in one stage, and the result is captured by the enabled dout flip-flop under new_data_rdy (1476/1486). After: unchanged — 0 register stages between the products and their sum, the same single dout flip-flop with the same new_data_rdy enable, the same output_data_ready logic and the same delay-line assignments. Latency and reset behaviour are identical; the rewrite adds no register, so nothing depends on an unknown initial value. The blocks are combinational and sit outside the always block, so they are evaluated every cycle and only dout's enable decides when the value is taken.

Why the rewrite computes the same value. Writing S06 = din + n_delay_reg6 (exact, 17 bits), a06 = S06[15:0], k06 = S06[16] and likewise for the other two pairs: C0*S06 = C0*a06 + 65536*C0*k06, so C0*a06 + C1*a15 + C2*a24 + C3*n_delay_reg3 + 65536*corr is exactly the original seven-term (six-term) sum, with corr = C0*k06 + C1*k15 + C2*k24. corr is at most 145 (f1), 209 (f2, h2), 237 (f3), 233 (h1), 174 (h3, h4), so {7'b0,corr,16'b0} fits bx's 32 bits. Every term is non-negative and the full sum is at most (sum of coefficients) x 65535 — 525x65535 = 3.44e7 for f1, 673x65535 = 4.41e7 for f2/h2, 474x65535 = 3.11e7 for f3, 466x65535 = 3.05e7 for h1, 348x65535 = 2.28e7 for h3/h4 — all below 2^28, so every partial result r1..r4 is below 2^32 (the bx chaining through result[31:0] loses nothing), the final 28-bit soft add does not carry out, and dout equals the original, which at those magnitudes is also exact in its 32-bit expression context. The carry correction is applied in all seven modules, not only where an input can reach 2^15, so the rewrite needs no assumption about the design's inputs; the extra cost is about 8 LUTs in each of the 24 instances that could have gone without it (roughly 0.5% of the area saved) and it does not change the worst stage, which is 11.10 ns either way.

No ASSUMES: line: the rewrite is correct for every 16-bit din.

Editor notes. Change only the seven my_fir_* module bodies. Keep the n_delay_reg1..6 shift chain, output_data_ready, the new_data_rdy enable and the else branch exactly as they are; keep using the `COEF* macros (the testbench passes them on the command line) rather than literal numbers. Declare the three 17-bit pair sums, the 9-bit corr and the 64-bit r1..r4 as wires at module scope, instantiate the blocks by port name (.ax, .ay, .bx, .result), and do not add a definition of comb_mult_add_16 to stereovision2.v — the model is supplied in sim_reference/comb_mult_add_16.v.

DESIGN_CHANGE: The carry correction is needed only because two vertical filters can wrap their 20-bit sign-extended accumulator: fltr_compute_f1 has coefficient 277 at line 862 and fltr_compute_h4 has 324 at line 1068, so at din=255 the partial product reaches 2^16, q4[16] is 1, line 867/1073 subtracts instead of adding, and dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] can reach about 58000 instead of its no-wrap bound (18200 for f1, 19061 for h4). If those filters held their partial products in a wider unsigned register (18-bit q with zero extension), every one of the seven filter outputs would be below 2^15 — 18200, 21451, 29190/8 = far below, 14981, 21451, 15427, 19061 — no pre-add in any my_fir module could carry, and the correction LUTs and the {7'b0,corr,16'b0} bx term could be dropped from all 42 instances, taking the worst stage from 11.10 ns to 10.03 ns.

1	// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
6	// reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_mult_add_16 (
8	    input  [15:0] ax,
9	    input  [15:0] ay,
10	    input  [31:0] bx,
11	    output [63:0] result
12	);
13	
14	    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
15	    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact
16	
17	    assign result = sum;
18	
19	endmodule

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

PLAN:

What is converted. All 45 candidate ids in the seven my_fir_* modules (lines 1486-1492, 1542-1548, 1602-1607, 1661-1666, 1716-1722, 1775-1780, 1833-1838). Each module's seven (or six) products are regrouped by the symmetry of its coefficients — C0=C6, C1=C5, C2=C4 in every one of the seven, verified against the `define blocks at 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798 — into three folded products plus, in f1/f2/h2, the centre tap. This is T2: the products are regrouped, no register is moved or added.

What is left, and why. All 46 fltr_compute_* ids (lines 859-865, 889-895, 928-934, 959-965, 992-998, 1030-1036, 1065-1071) are left, for three reasons that apply to every one of them:

  1. Tile cost. These are 8x9 constant products packed four to a DSP tile; a comb_mult_add_16 takes a tile alone. Even folded by symmetry (these coefficient sets are symmetric too) they would need 25 blocks per v_fltr instance, 150 blocks, 150 extra tiles. With the 144 blocks of this plan the design would need more than the device's 306 tiles, and the added DSP area (150 x 253779 = 3.8e7) far exceeds the ~20-bit soft adder trees it would remove.
  2. Register position. The table's "products registered 1 stage before the sum" matches lines 859-867: q1..q7 are registered, the sum is in the next stage. A combinational mult-add can only absorb that sum by retiming a register across the 56-bit din port (56 added flip-flops per instance), which is outside what the rewrite needs.
  3. Signedness. The sum at 867/897/936/967/1000/1038/1073 sign-extends each 17-bit q ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}) and wraps mod 2^20. The block is unsigned, so each term whose q[16] can be 1 — which happens in fltr_compute_f1 (line 862, coefficient 277: 255*277 = 70635) and fltr_compute_h4 (line 1068, coefficient 324: 255*324 = 82620) — would need an explicit -2^17 correction term per product on top of everything else.

Blocks and tiles. 4 blocks in each of my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2 and 3 blocks in each of my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4 = 24 per h_fltr instance, x6 instances = 144 blocks. They replace all 270 two_mult_18x19 multiplies of the my_fir modules (45 per h_fltr x 6), which at two to a tile occupy about 135 tiles; 224 - 135 + 144 = 233 tiles, inside the 306 the device has. The 57 tiles holding the 9x9 fltr_compute products are untouched. Net DSP area +9 x 253779 = +2.3e6 (+2.3%); the soft logic removed is larger (below), so total logic-block area falls.

Longest series of blocks, and the stage. Two blocks, never more: mul_a->mul_b, and mul_c->mul_d (7-tap) or mul_c alone (6-tap), the two chains joined by one 28-bit soft adder. Worst stage, 7-tap with the correction (my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2): flip-flop 0.060 + pre-adder level 1.069 + correction LUT 1.069 + wire into block 1.419 + block 2.14 + block-to-block wire 1.17 + block 2.14 + wire into soft logic 0.960 + final 28-bit adder level 1.069 = 11.10 ns, against the baseline slowest stage 11.6069 ns. The same stage without the correction LUT on it (the s24 data path, and the whole of the four 6-tap modules) is 10.03 ns; the correction path in a 6-tap module is 7.79 ns, since mul_c there feeds the final adder directly. Both baseline paths 1 and 2 are my_fir stages of the identical shape (one DSP multiply, six adder levels, one LUT, enabled flip-flop) and all 42 my_fir instances share that shape, so every stage between 11.293 and 11.6069 ns is rewritten; the period after the rewrite is set either by this 11.10 ns stage or by an untouched stage at or below 11.293 ns.

Soft logic that leaves, and from which stage. Out of each my_fir stage (the stage that holds baseline paths 1 and 2, the slowest and second slowest): the 6-deep 28-bit adder chain (5-deep in the 6-tap modules), i.e. about 168 adder cells per 7-tap instance and 140 per 6-tap instance. Into it: three 16-bit pre-adders (48 cells), one 28-bit final adder (28 cells) and the correction LUTs (about 8). Net about 84 cells saved per 7-tap instance and 56 per 6-tap, 476 per h_fltr instance, about 2900 cells over the six instances — on the order of 290 clusters, 8e6 area units, roughly 8% of the 9.73e7 baseline, against the +2.3e6 of DSP. Fewer 28-bit nets in the adder trees should also shorten routed wirelength. No other stage gains logic: the pre-adders and the correction LUT sit in the same stage the adder tree left.

Register stages, before and after. For every converted region, before: the operands din and n_delay_reg1..6 (lines 1467-1472, 1478-1483 and the matching lines in each module) are flip-flop outputs, the product and the whole sum are combinational in one stage, and the result is captured by the enabled dout flip-flop under new_data_rdy (1476/1486). After: unchanged — 0 register stages between the products and their sum, the same single dout flip-flop with the same new_data_rdy enable, the same output_data_ready logic and the same delay-line assignments. Latency and reset behaviour are identical; the rewrite adds no register, so nothing depends on an unknown initial value. The blocks are combinational and sit outside the always block, so they are evaluated every cycle and only dout's enable decides when the value is taken.

Why the rewrite computes the same value. Writing S06 = din + n_delay_reg6 (exact, 17 bits), a06 = S06[15:0], k06 = S06[16] and likewise for the other two pairs: C0*S06 = C0*a06 + 65536*C0*k06, so C0*a06 + C1*a15 + C2*a24 + C3*n_delay_reg3 + 65536*corr is exactly the original seven-term (six-term) sum, with corr = C0*k06 + C1*k15 + C2*k24. corr is at most 145 (f1), 209 (f2, h2), 237 (f3), 233 (h1), 174 (h3, h4), so {7'b0,corr,16'b0} fits bx's 32 bits. Every term is non-negative and the full sum is at most (sum of coefficients) x 65535 — 525x65535 = 3.44e7 for f1, 673x65535 = 4.41e7 for f2/h2, 474x65535 = 3.11e7 for f3, 466x65535 = 3.05e7 for h1, 348x65535 = 2.28e7 for h3/h4 — all below 2^28, so every partial result r1..r4 is below 2^32 (the bx chaining through result[31:0] loses nothing), the final 28-bit soft add does not carry out, and dout equals the original, which at those magnitudes is also exact in its 32-bit expression context. The carry correction is applied in all seven modules, not only where an input can reach 2^15, so the rewrite needs no assumption about the design's inputs; the extra cost is about 8 LUTs in each of the 24 instances that could have gone without it (roughly 0.5% of the area saved) and it does not change the worst stage, which is 11.10 ns either way.

No ASSUMES: line: the rewrite is correct for every 16-bit din.

Editor notes. Change only the seven my_fir_* module bodies. Keep the n_delay_reg1..6 shift chain, output_data_ready, the new_data_rdy enable and the else branch exactly as they are; keep using the `COEF* macros (the testbench passes them on the command line) rather than literal numbers. Declare the three 17-bit pair sums, the 9-bit corr and the 64-bit r1..r4 as wires at module scope, instantiate the blocks by port name (.ax, .ay, .bx, .result), and do not add a definition of comb_mult_add_16 to stereovision2.v — the model is supplied in sim_reference/comb_mult_add_16.v.

DESIGN_CHANGE: The carry correction is needed only because two vertical filters can wrap their 20-bit sign-extended accumulator: fltr_compute_f1 has coefficient 277 at line 862 and fltr_compute_h4 has 324 at line 1068, so at din=255 the partial product reaches 2^16, q4[16] is 1, line 867/1073 subtracts instead of adding, and dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] can reach about 58000 instead of its no-wrap bound (18200 for f1, 19061 for h4). If those filters held their partial products in a wider unsigned register (18-bit q with zero extension), every one of the seven filter outputs would be below 2^15 — 18200, 21451, 29190/8 = far below, 14981, 21451, 15427, 19061 — no pre-add in any my_fir module could carry, and the correction LUTs and the {7'b0,corr,16'b0} bx term could be dropped from all 42 instances, taking the worst stage from 11.10 ns to 10.03 ns.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_mult_add_16.v) are in sim_reference/.

1	// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
6	// reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_mult_add_16 (
8	    input  [15:0] ax,
9	    input  [15:0] ay,
10	    input  [31:0] bx,
11	    output [63:0] result
12	);
13	
14	    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
15	    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact
16	
17	    assign result = sum;
18

PLAN:

What is converted. All 45 candidate ids in the seven my_fir_* modules (lines 1486-1492, 1542-1548, 1602-1607, 1661-1666, 1716-1722, 1775-1780, 1833-1838). Each module's seven (or six) products are regrouped by the symmetry of its coefficients — C0=C6, C1=C5, C2=C4 in every one of the seven, verified against the `define blocks at 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798 — into three folded products plus, in f1/f2/h2, the centre tap. This is T2: the products are regrouped, no register is moved or added.

What is left, and why. All 46 fltr_compute_* ids (lines 859-865, 889-895, 928-934, 959-965, 992-998, 1030-1036, 1065-1071) are left, for three reasons that apply to every one of them:

  1. Tile cost. These are 8x9 constant products packed four to a DSP tile; a comb_mult_add_16 takes a tile alone. Even folded by symmetry (these coefficient sets are symmetric too) they would need 25 blocks per v_fltr instance, 150 blocks, 150 extra tiles. With the 144 blocks of this plan the design would need more than the device's 306 tiles, and the added DSP area (150 x 253779 = 3.8e7) far exceeds the ~20-bit soft adder trees it would remove.
  2. Register position. The table's "products registered 1 stage before the sum" matches lines 859-867: q1..q7 are registered, the sum is in the next stage. A combinational mult-add can only absorb that sum by retiming a register across the 56-bit din port (56 added flip-flops per instance), which is outside what the rewrite needs.
  3. Signedness. The sum at 867/897/936/967/1000/1038/1073 sign-extends each 17-bit q ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}) and wraps mod 2^20. The block is unsigned, so each term whose q[16] can be 1 — which happens in fltr_compute_f1 (line 862, coefficient 277: 255*277 = 70635) and fltr_compute_h4 (line 1068, coefficient 324: 255*324 = 82620) — would need an explicit -2^17 correction term per product on top of everything else.

Blocks and tiles. 4 blocks in each of my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2 and 3 blocks in each of my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4 = 24 per h_fltr instance, x6 instances = 144 blocks. They replace all 270 two_mult_18x19 multiplies of the my_fir modules (45 per h_fltr x 6), which at two to a tile occupy about 135 tiles; 224 - 135 + 144 = 233 tiles, inside the 306 the device has. The 57 tiles holding the 9x9 fltr_compute products are untouched. Net DSP area +9 x 253779 = +2.3e6 (+2.3%); the soft logic removed is larger (below), so total logic-block area falls.

Longest series of blocks, and the stage. Two blocks, never more: mul_a->mul_b, and mul_c->mul_d (7-tap) or mul_c alone (6-tap), the two chains joined by one 28-bit soft adder. Worst stage, 7-tap with the correction (my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2): flip-flop 0.060 + pre-adder level 1.069 + correction LUT 1.069 + wire into block 1.419 + block 2.14 + block-to-block wire 1.17 + block 2.14 + wire into soft logic 0.960 + final 28-bit adder level 1.069 = 11.10 ns, against the baseline slowest stage 11.6069 ns. The same stage without the correction LUT on it (the s24 data path, and the whole of the four 6-tap modules) is 10.03 ns; the correction path in a 6-tap module is 7.79 ns, since mul_c there feeds the final adder directly. Both baseline paths 1 and 2 are my_fir stages of the identical shape (one DSP multiply, six adder levels, one LUT, enabled flip-flop) and all 42 my_fir instances share that shape, so every stage between 11.293 and 11.6069 ns is rewritten; the period after the rewrite is set either by this 11.10 ns stage or by an untouched stage at or below 11.293 ns.

Soft logic that leaves, and from which stage. Out of each my_fir stage (the stage that holds baseline paths 1 and 2, the slowest and second slowest): the 6-deep 28-bit adder chain (5-deep in the 6-tap modules), i.e. about 168 adder cells per 7-tap instance and 140 per 6-tap instance. Into it: three 16-bit pre-adders (48 cells), one 28-bit final adder (28 cells) and the correction LUTs (about 8). Net about 84 cells saved per 7-tap instance and 56 per 6-tap, 476 per h_fltr instance, about 2900 cells over the six instances — on the order of 290 clusters, 8e6 area units, roughly 8% of the 9.73e7 baseline, against the +2.3e6 of DSP. Fewer 28-bit nets in the adder trees should also shorten routed wirelength. No other stage gains logic: the pre-adders and the correction LUT sit in the same stage the adder tree left.

Register stages, before and after. For every converted region, before: the operands din and n_delay_reg1..6 (lines 1467-1472, 1478-1483 and the matching lines in each module) are flip-flop outputs, the product and the whole sum are combinational in one stage, and the result is captured by the enabled dout flip-flop under new_data_rdy (1476/1486). After: unchanged — 0 register stages between the products and their sum, the same single dout flip-flop with the same new_data_rdy enable, the same output_data_ready logic and the same delay-line assignments. Latency and reset behaviour are identical; the rewrite adds no register, so nothing depends on an unknown initial value. The blocks are combinational and sit outside the always block, so they are evaluated every cycle and only dout's enable decides when the value is taken.

Why the rewrite computes the same value. Writing S06 = din + n_delay_reg6 (exact, 17 bits), a06 = S06[15:0], k06 = S06[16] and likewise for the other two pairs: C0*S06 = C0*a06 + 65536*C0*k06, so C0*a06 + C1*a15 + C2*a24 + C3*n_delay_reg3 + 65536*corr is exactly the original seven-term (six-term) sum, with corr = C0*k06 + C1*k15 + C2*k24. corr is at most 145 (f1), 209 (f2, h2), 237 (f3), 233 (h1), 174 (h3, h4), so {7'b0,corr,16'b0} fits bx's 32 bits. Every term is non-negative and the full sum is at most (sum of coefficients) x 65535 — 525x65535 = 3.44e7 for f1, 673x65535 = 4.41e7 for f2/h2, 474x65535 = 3.11e7 for f3, 466x65535 = 3.05e7 for h1, 348x65535 = 2.28e7 for h3/h4 — all below 2^28, so every partial result r1..r4 is below 2^32 (the bx chaining through result[31:0] loses nothing), the final 28-bit soft add does not carry out, and dout equals the original, which at those magnitudes is also exact in its 32-bit expression context. The carry correction is applied in all seven modules, not only where an input can reach 2^15, so the rewrite needs no assumption about the design's inputs; the extra cost is about 8 LUTs in each of the 24 instances that could have gone without it (roughly 0.5% of the area saved) and it does not change the worst stage, which is 11.10 ns either way.

No ASSUMES: line: the rewrite is correct for every 16-bit din.

Keep the n_delay_reg1..6 shift chain, output_data_ready, the new_data_rdy enable and the else branch exactly as they are; keep using the `COEF* macros (the testbench passes them on the command line) rather than literal numbers. Declare the three 17-bit pair sums, the 9-bit corr and the 64-bit r1..r4 as wires at module scope, instantiate the blocks by port name (.ax, .ay, .bx, .result), and do not add a definition of comb_mult_add_16 to stereovision2.v — the model is supplied in sim_reference/comb_mult_add_16.v.

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_mult_add_16.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

response

I'll start by reading the design and the supporting files.

Now I'll rewrite the seven my_fir_* modules. Starting with my_fir_f1:

Now my_fir_f3 (6-tap, no centre term):

Let me verify behavioural equivalence of one 7-tap and one 6-tap module by simulation.

check.sh passes and the census shows exactly the 144 comb_mult_add_16 instances the plan calls for. An independent iverilog run (200 000 cycles, all seven modules against unmodified reference copies, including a 0xFFFF stretch that forces every pair-sum carry) reports no mismatch on dout or output_data_ready.

What changed, region by region

All 45 regions are the $mul cells of the dout sums in the seven my_fir_* modules. Every one was removed and regrouped by coefficient symmetry (C0=C6, C1=C5, C2=C4 in all seven) onto the block. Nothing else in the file was touched — the n_delay_reg1..6 shift chain, the new_data_rdy enable, output_data_ready and the else branch are byte-identical.

Per module I added, at module scope, c0..c2 (and c3 where a centre tap exists) as 16-bit localparams fed from the module's own `COEF* macros, the three 17-bit folded pair sums s06/s15/s24, a 9-bit corr, and 64-bit r1..r4.

  • my_fir_f1 (regions …1486$154……1492$165, coefficients _b): 4 blocks. mul_a(s06[15:0], c0, 0), mul_b(s15[15:0], c1, r1[31:0]), mul_c(s24[15:0], c2, {7'b0,corr,16'b0}), mul_d(n_delay_reg3, c3, r3[31:0]); dout <= r2[27:0] + r4[27:0].
  • my_fir_f2 (…1542$169……1548$180, _c): same 4-block shape.
  • my_fir_h2 (…1716$210……1722$221, _2): same 4-block shape.
  • my_fir_f3 (…1602$184……1607$193, _d), my_fir_h1 (…1661$197……1666$206, _1), my_fir_h3 (…1775$225……1780$234, _3), my_fir_h4 (…1833$238……1838$247, _4): 3 blocks each (these six-tap modules have no centre term); dout <= r2[27:0] + r3[27:0].

corr = (s06[16]?c0:0) + (s15[16]?c1:0) + (s24[16]?c2:0) restores the 2^16 weight that ax drops when a pair sum carries, so C0*s06 + C1*s15 + C2*s24 + C3*nd3 is reproduced exactly. It is applied in all seven modules, so the rewrite holds for every 16-bit din — no ASSUMES: line. Every partial result stays below 2^28 (worst case 673·65535 = 4.41e7 in f2/h2), so chaining through bx as result[31:0] and the final 28-bit soft add lose nothing.

Register structure is unchanged: 0 stages between the products and their sum, the same single enabled dout flip-flop. The blocks are combinational and sit outside the always block, and the rewrite adds no register, so nothing depends on an unknown initial value.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
// reaches result in the same cycle.
module comb_mult_add_16 (
    input  [15:0] ax,
    input  [15:0] ay,
    input  [31:0] bx,
    output [63:0] result
);

    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact

    assign result = sum;

endmodule
