Task

You are the acceptance reviewer. You did not plan or write this edit. Check the edit against the approved plan, the block's contract and the correctness rules.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_mult_add_16 (precision INT16)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx
  • input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The design

The file stereovision2.v is the edited design. The edit is the diff below, taken against the original source.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.

PLAN:

What is converted. All 45 candidate ids in the seven my_fir_* modules (lines 1486-1492, 1542-1548, 1602-1607, 1661-1666, 1716-1722, 1775-1780, 1833-1838). Each module's seven (or six) products are regrouped by the symmetry of its coefficients — C0=C6, C1=C5, C2=C4 in every one of the seven, verified against the `define blocks at 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798 — into three folded products plus, in f1/f2/h2, the centre tap. This is T2: the products are regrouped, no register is moved or added.

What is left, and why. All 46 fltr_compute_* ids (lines 859-865, 889-895, 928-934, 959-965, 992-998, 1030-1036, 1065-1071) are left, for three reasons that apply to every one of them:

  1. Tile cost. These are 8x9 constant products packed four to a DSP tile; a comb_mult_add_16 takes a tile alone. Even folded by symmetry (these coefficient sets are symmetric too) they would need 25 blocks per v_fltr instance, 150 blocks, 150 extra tiles. With the 144 blocks of this plan the design would need more than the device's 306 tiles, and the added DSP area (150 x 253779 = 3.8e7) far exceeds the ~20-bit soft adder trees it would remove.
  2. Register position. The table's "products registered 1 stage before the sum" matches lines 859-867: q1..q7 are registered, the sum is in the next stage. A combinational mult-add can only absorb that sum by retiming a register across the 56-bit din port (56 added flip-flops per instance), which is outside what the rewrite needs.
  3. Signedness. The sum at 867/897/936/967/1000/1038/1073 sign-extends each 17-bit q ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}) and wraps mod 2^20. The block is unsigned, so each term whose q[16] can be 1 — which happens in fltr_compute_f1 (line 862, coefficient 277: 255*277 = 70635) and fltr_compute_h4 (line 1068, coefficient 324: 255*324 = 82620) — would need an explicit -2^17 correction term per product on top of everything else.

Blocks and tiles. 4 blocks in each of my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2 and 3 blocks in each of my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4 = 24 per h_fltr instance, x6 instances = 144 blocks. They replace all 270 two_mult_18x19 multiplies of the my_fir modules (45 per h_fltr x 6), which at two to a tile occupy about 135 tiles; 224 - 135 + 144 = 233 tiles, inside the 306 the device has. The 57 tiles holding the 9x9 fltr_compute products are untouched. Net DSP area +9 x 253779 = +2.3e6 (+2.3%); the soft logic removed is larger (below), so total logic-block area falls.

Longest series of blocks, and the stage. Two blocks, never more: mul_a->mul_b, and mul_c->mul_d (7-tap) or mul_c alone (6-tap), the two chains joined by one 28-bit soft adder. Worst stage, 7-tap with the correction (my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2): flip-flop 0.060 + pre-adder level 1.069 + correction LUT 1.069 + wire into block 1.419 + block 2.14 + block-to-block wire 1.17 + block 2.14 + wire into soft logic 0.960 + final 28-bit adder level 1.069 = 11.10 ns, against the baseline slowest stage 11.6069 ns. The same stage without the correction LUT on it (the s24 data path, and the whole of the four 6-tap modules) is 10.03 ns; the correction path in a 6-tap module is 7.79 ns, since mul_c there feeds the final adder directly. Both baseline paths 1 and 2 are my_fir stages of the identical shape (one DSP multiply, six adder levels, one LUT, enabled flip-flop) and all 42 my_fir instances share that shape, so every stage between 11.293 and 11.6069 ns is rewritten; the period after the rewrite is set either by this 11.10 ns stage or by an untouched stage at or below 11.293 ns.

Soft logic that leaves, and from which stage. Out of each my_fir stage (the stage that holds baseline paths 1 and 2, the slowest and second slowest): the 6-deep 28-bit adder chain (5-deep in the 6-tap modules), i.e. about 168 adder cells per 7-tap instance and 140 per 6-tap instance. Into it: three 16-bit pre-adders (48 cells), one 28-bit final adder (28 cells) and the correction LUTs (about 8). Net about 84 cells saved per 7-tap instance and 56 per 6-tap, 476 per h_fltr instance, about 2900 cells over the six instances — on the order of 290 clusters, 8e6 area units, roughly 8% of the 9.73e7 baseline, against the +2.3e6 of DSP. Fewer 28-bit nets in the adder trees should also shorten routed wirelength. No other stage gains logic: the pre-adders and the correction LUT sit in the same stage the adder tree left.

Register stages, before and after. For every converted region, before: the operands din and n_delay_reg1..6 (lines 1467-1472, 1478-1483 and the matching lines in each module) are flip-flop outputs, the product and the whole sum are combinational in one stage, and the result is captured by the enabled dout flip-flop under new_data_rdy (1476/1486). After: unchanged — 0 register stages between the products and their sum, the same single dout flip-flop with the same new_data_rdy enable, the same output_data_ready logic and the same delay-line assignments. Latency and reset behaviour are identical; the rewrite adds no register, so nothing depends on an unknown initial value. The blocks are combinational and sit outside the always block, so they are evaluated every cycle and only dout's enable decides when the value is taken.

Why the rewrite computes the same value. Writing S06 = din + n_delay_reg6 (exact, 17 bits), a06 = S06[15:0], k06 = S06[16] and likewise for the other two pairs: C0*S06 = C0*a06 + 65536*C0*k06, so C0*a06 + C1*a15 + C2*a24 + C3*n_delay_reg3 + 65536*corr is exactly the original seven-term (six-term) sum, with corr = C0*k06 + C1*k15 + C2*k24. corr is at most 145 (f1), 209 (f2, h2), 237 (f3), 233 (h1), 174 (h3, h4), so {7'b0,corr,16'b0} fits bx's 32 bits. Every term is non-negative and the full sum is at most (sum of coefficients) x 65535 — 525x65535 = 3.44e7 for f1, 673x65535 = 4.41e7 for f2/h2, 474x65535 = 3.11e7 for f3, 466x65535 = 3.05e7 for h1, 348x65535 = 2.28e7 for h3/h4 — all below 2^28, so every partial result r1..r4 is below 2^32 (the bx chaining through result[31:0] loses nothing), the final 28-bit soft add does not carry out, and dout equals the original, which at those magnitudes is also exact in its 32-bit expression context. The carry correction is applied in all seven modules, not only where an input can reach 2^15, so the rewrite needs no assumption about the design's inputs; the extra cost is about 8 LUTs in each of the 24 instances that could have gone without it (roughly 0.5% of the area saved) and it does not change the worst stage, which is 11.10 ns either way.

No ASSUMES: line: the rewrite is correct for every 16-bit din.

Editor notes. Change only the seven my_fir_* module bodies. Keep the n_delay_reg1..6 shift chain, output_data_ready, the new_data_rdy enable and the else branch exactly as they are; keep using the `COEF* macros (the testbench passes them on the command line) rather than literal numbers. Declare the three 17-bit pair sums, the 9-bit corr and the 64-bit r1..r4 as wires at module scope, instantiate the blocks by port name (.ax, .ay, .bx, .result), and do not add a definition of comb_mult_add_16 to stereovision2.v — the model is supplied in sim_reference/comb_mult_add_16.v.

DESIGN_CHANGE: The carry correction is needed only because two vertical filters can wrap their 20-bit sign-extended accumulator: fltr_compute_f1 has coefficient 277 at line 862 and fltr_compute_h4 has 324 at line 1068, so at din=255 the partial product reaches 2^16, q4[16] is 1, line 867/1073 subtracts instead of adding, and dout = d_out_tmp[18:3] can reach about 58000 instead of its no-wrap bound (18200 for f1, 19061 for h4). If those filters held their partial products in a wider unsigned register (18-bit q with zero extension), every one of the seven filter outputs would be below 2^15 — 18200, 21451, 29190/8 = far below, 14981, 21451, 15427, 19061 — no pre-add in any my_fir module could carry, and the correction LUTs and the {7'b0,corr,16'b0} bx term could be dropped from all 42 instances, taking the worst stage from 11.10 ns to 10.03 ns.

No comb_mult_add_16 definition was added; 24 instantiations, matching the log.
  • Ports. Every instance connects .ax, .ay, .bx, .result by name; ay is a 16-bit localparam from the module's own `COEF macros, bx is 32 bits in all four forms (32'b0, r1[31:0], {7'b0,corr,16'b0}, r3[31:0]), result into 64-bit wires. mul_d present exactly in the three modules whose COEF3 is nonzero (f1, f2, h2).

The ax ports drop only bit 16 of each 17-bit pair sum, and corr<<16 restores it; corr peaks at 237 (f3), inside its 9 bits, and c*[8:0] is lossless for coefficients ≤255. Every r* stays below 2^32 (worst 4.3e7), so r1[31:0]/r3[31:0] chaining is exact, and the final 28-bit add equals the original 32-bit sum truncated to dout's 28 bits.

  • Assumptions. The correction is applied in all seven modules, so no ASSUMES: line is needed, and none is claimed.

1	// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
6	// reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_mult_add_16 (
8	    input  [15:0] ax,
9	    input  [15:0] ay,
10	    input  [31:0] bx,
11	    output [63:0] result
12	);
13	
14	    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
15	    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact
16	
17	    assign result = sum;
18	
19	endmodule

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_mult_add_16 (precision INT16)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx
  • input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The design

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (channel width 300, median of five seeds, 1 to 5) has a worst register-to-register path of 11.6069 ns on its one clock tm3_clk_v0 (I/O pads not timed) and uses 224 DSP tiles (as packed at seed 1) of the device's 306. Its used logic-block area is 9.73358e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905) and its routed wirelength is 436921, so its area x delay x wirelength product, the objective, is 4.93619e+14. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • The block's internal delay is fixed. Soft logic between a block's output and the next register adds to that stage; blocks in series each add their delay plus a wire.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.

PLAN:

This is a revision of the kept candidate. It keeps the same 144 blocks and the same symmetric folding, and changes two things that cost it 2.9 ns of carry chain in front of the blocks and 2.1 ns + 1.17 ns of block-to-block wire inside the stage:

  1. The carry correction is removed from the critical path by halving instead of truncating. The kept candidate fed ax = s[15:0] and had to add back the dropped bit 16 with corr = (s06[16]?c0:0)+(s15[16]?c1:0)+(s24[16]?c2:0), whose three terms depend on the carry out of the 17-bit pair adder: the seed-1 report shows that as $add~226 (5 stages) + $add~227 (1 stage) with their wires, 2.962 ns between the pair sum and the first block. Instead feed ax = s[16:1] (the full 17-bit sum shifted right by one, no bits lost) and ay = 2*c. Then ax*ay = (s>>1)*2c = s*c - s[0]*c, and the only missing term is s[0]*c, where s[0] = x[0]^y[0] is one XOR of two tap-register bits — it does not wait on the carry chain. The three missing terms are summed into one 9-bit corr written as a case over the three bits {p0,p1,p2} with constant arms, so each corr bit is a 3-input function, one LUT level, not an adder; corr is placed in mul_a's otherwise-unused bx. corr <= c0+c1+c2 <= 237 for every module, so it fits in 9 bits.
  2. The two block-to-block chains are broken. The kept candidate chained mul_a→mul_b and mul_c→mul_d through bx, putting two blocks plus a 1.17 ns block-to-block wire in one stage (2.140+1.170+2.140 = 5.45 ns). Here all four blocks run in parallel with bx tied to 0 (or to corr on mul_a) and their results are summed in a two-level soft adder tree of 28-bit adds. That trades 2 extra adders per 7-tap instance and 1 per 6-tap instance (60 extra 28-bit adds, about 1680 BLEs, roughly +5% used logic area) for 1.57 ns off the stage, about -14% on the period; the product moves in our favour because the baseline's two slowest stages both live in these modules, so no other stage holds the period up near 11 ns.

Correctness of the arithmetic, per module. The seven coefficient sets are symmetric (COEF0=COEF6, COEF1=COEF5, COEF2=COEF4; lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), so din*c0 + n_delay_reg6*c6 = s06*c0 and likewise for the other two pairs; COEF3 is 0 in f3/h1/h3/h4 and those sums have only six products, which is why those modules get three blocks and no mul_d. Summing the four (three) block results:
r_a + r_b + r_c (+ r_d) = s06*c0 + s15*c1 + s24*c2 (+ n_delay_reg3*c3) - (p0*c0 + p1*c1 + p2*c2) + corr, and corr is exactly that subtracted amount, so the total is the original sum term for term. All operands are unsigned and no value wraps: ax <= 65535, ay = 2*c <= 510 (both inside their 16-bit ports), each result <= 65535*510 + 237 < 2^26 (inside bx's 32 bits where it is reused, and far inside result's 64 bits), and the full sum is at most 65535*673 = 44.1e6 < 2^28, so the original 28-bit dout never truncated and the [27:0] slices of the block results lose nothing. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line: the halving identity holds for every 16-bit din, including the one module (my_fir_f3, fed from fltr_compute_f3 whose coefficient sum 1126*255 = 287130 can set bit 18 of d_out_tmp, line 936-937) whose din really can have bit 15 set.

Everything else in the my_fir modules is untouched: the tap shift register, the new_data_rdy enable on dout and on the taps, output_data_ready, and the else branch. The blocks are combinational and sit entirely inside the existing register-to-register stage, so no register is added, moved or removed, and no value that leaves the module goes inside a block — the only readers of the products are the dout sum itself (lines 1486-1492 and the matching lines in the other six modules), and the taps keep their own wires for the shift register.

Register stages, per converted region, before and after: before, each product is combinational from the tap registers (or din, itself a register output in h_fltr's source) into the same-cycle adder chain and lands in dout — 0 register stages between product and sum, 1 register stage from operand to result. After, the operand registers feed a 17-bit pair adder, one block, two soft adder levels and dout — still 0 register stages between product and sum and 1 from operand to result, so dout, output_data_ready and every downstream h_fltr/steer_fltr register keep their cycle-by-cycle values.

Blocks and tiles: 24 blocks per h_fltr instance (4 each for f1, f2, h2; 3 each for f3, h1, h3, h4) times 6 h_fltr instances = 144 blocks, unchanged from the kept candidate. Each takes a DSP tile alone; the 42 fltr_compute instances keep their 57 tiles of mult_9x9_fixed_pt, so the design uses 201 tiles, as packing measured for the kept candidate at seed 1, against the baseline's 224.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block's bx is driven by another block, so the only block delay in the stage is 2.140 ns, against 5.450 ns of block-plus-wire in the kept candidate. The stage this rewrite leaves, using the seed-1 numbers from the kept candidate's own report for the same elements: 0.103 (clock to tap-register output) + 0.792 wire + 0.474 seventeen-stage pair-sum carry chain = 1.369; + 1.001 register-to-block wire + 2.140 block = 4.510; + 0.544 block-into-soft-logic wire + 0.778 twenty-eight-stage adder = 5.832; + 0.960 wire + 0.778 second adder level = 7.570; + 1.807 wire + 0.153 enable LUT = 9.530, plus 0.019 setup. The corr side path is 0.103 + 0.960 wire + 0.153 LUT = 1.216, + 1.001 wire = 2.217 at mul_a's bx, which is earlier than ax at 2.370, so the correction is off the critical path. The 7-tap mul_d side path is 0.103 + 1.419 register-to-block wire + 2.140 = 3.662, also slack. So the rewrite's stage is about 9.6 ns against the baseline's slowest stage of 11.6069 ns and its second slowest of 11.293 ns — and both of those stages are inside converted modules (my_fir_f1 and my_fir_f2), so they no longer exist. The slowest stage left outside the converted modules is fltr_compute's d_out_tmp sum: registered 9x9 products into six 20-bit adder levels, about 0.1 + 6x1.069 + a last wire, roughly 7.5-8.5 ns, below this stage; steer_fltr's deepest stage (im_p_tmp, lines 641/643) is four 31-bit terms, three adder levels, about 4 ns. So 9.6 ns is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves.

Soft logic leaving the stage: in each my_fir instance the six (or five) 28-bit adder levels of the original reduction go away, replaced by three 17-bit pair adders, nine corr LUTs and two 28-bit adder levels; seven (or six) hard multiplies become four (or three) blocks. That stage was the baseline's slowest and second slowest, so the removal is where the period comes from; the added soft adder level relative to the kept candidate is paid for by removing a block and a block-to-block wire from the same stage.

Candidates left, with reasons:

  • All 46 fltr_compute candidate rows (fltr_compute_f1 lines 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071), each 6 instances, are left. Three reasons, all of them sufficient. (a) Tiles: they are 8-bit by constant products packed four to a mult_9x9_fixed_pt tile, 294 products on 57 tiles; a block takes a tile alone, so converting even one module's seven products would cost about 5 extra tiles per instance, and converting all of them would need hundreds of tiles against a 306-tile device. (b) Their products are registered one stage before the sum (q1..q7, line 867 and its counterparts), so the block's adder cannot absorb the d_out_tmp reduction without deleting those registers and moving the whole 7-term sum into the multiply stage, which lengthens that stage and changes nothing on the critical path. (c) Their stage is roughly 7.5-8.5 ns, well under the slowest stage, so nothing bought there helps the period while every block added costs a tile (about 9 CLBs).
  • No my_fir candidate is left: all 46 rows across the seven modules are converted.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

PLAN:

This is a revision of the kept candidate. It keeps the same 144 blocks and the same symmetric folding, and changes two things that cost it 2.9 ns of carry chain in front of the blocks and 2.1 ns + 1.17 ns of block-to-block wire inside the stage:

  1. The carry correction is removed from the critical path by halving instead of truncating. The kept candidate fed ax = s[15:0] and had to add back the dropped bit 16 with corr = (s06[16]?c0:0)+(s15[16]?c1:0)+(s24[16]?c2:0), whose three terms depend on the carry out of the 17-bit pair adder: the seed-1 report shows that as $add~226 (5 stages) + $add~227 (1 stage) with their wires, 2.962 ns between the pair sum and the first block. Instead feed ax = s[16:1] (the full 17-bit sum shifted right by one, no bits lost) and ay = 2*c. Then ax*ay = (s>>1)*2c = s*c - s[0]*c, and the only missing term is s[0]*c, where s[0] = x[0]^y[0] is one XOR of two tap-register bits — it does not wait on the carry chain. The three missing terms are summed into one 9-bit corr written as a case over the three bits {p0,p1,p2} with constant arms, so each corr bit is a 3-input function, one LUT level, not an adder; corr is placed in mul_a's otherwise-unused bx. corr <= c0+c1+c2 <= 237 for every module, so it fits in 9 bits.
  2. The two block-to-block chains are broken. The kept candidate chained mul_a→mul_b and mul_c→mul_d through bx, putting two blocks plus a 1.17 ns block-to-block wire in one stage (2.140+1.170+2.140 = 5.45 ns). Here all four blocks run in parallel with bx tied to 0 (or to corr on mul_a) and their results are summed in a two-level soft adder tree of 28-bit adds. That trades 2 extra adders per 7-tap instance and 1 per 6-tap instance (60 extra 28-bit adds, about 1680 BLEs, roughly +5% used logic area) for 1.57 ns off the stage, about -14% on the period; the product moves in our favour because the baseline's two slowest stages both live in these modules, so no other stage holds the period up near 11 ns.

Correctness of the arithmetic, per module. The seven coefficient sets are symmetric (COEF0=COEF6, COEF1=COEF5, COEF2=COEF4; lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), so din*c0 + n_delay_reg6*c6 = s06*c0 and likewise for the other two pairs; COEF3 is 0 in f3/h1/h3/h4 and those sums have only six products, which is why those modules get three blocks and no mul_d. Summing the four (three) block results:
r_a + r_b + r_c (+ r_d) = s06*c0 + s15*c1 + s24*c2 (+ n_delay_reg3*c3) - (p0*c0 + p1*c1 + p2*c2) + corr, and corr is exactly that subtracted amount, so the total is the original sum term for term. All operands are unsigned and no value wraps: ax <= 65535, ay = 2*c <= 510 (both inside their 16-bit ports), each result <= 65535*510 + 237 < 2^26 (inside bx's 32 bits where it is reused, and far inside result's 64 bits), and the full sum is at most 65535*673 = 44.1e6 < 2^28, so the original 28-bit dout never truncated and the [27:0] slices of the block results lose nothing. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line: the halving identity holds for every 16-bit din, including the one module (my_fir_f3, fed from fltr_compute_f3 whose coefficient sum 1126*255 = 287130 can set bit 18 of d_out_tmp, line 936-937) whose din really can have bit 15 set.

Everything else in the my_fir modules is untouched: the tap shift register, the new_data_rdy enable on dout and on the taps, output_data_ready, and the else branch. The blocks are combinational and sit entirely inside the existing register-to-register stage, so no register is added, moved or removed, and no value that leaves the module goes inside a block — the only readers of the products are the dout sum itself (lines 1486-1492 and the matching lines in the other six modules), and the taps keep their own wires for the shift register.

Register stages, per converted region, before and after: before, each product is combinational from the tap registers (or din, itself a register output in h_fltr's source) into the same-cycle adder chain and lands in dout — 0 register stages between product and sum, 1 register stage from operand to result. After, the operand registers feed a 17-bit pair adder, one block, two soft adder levels and dout — still 0 register stages between product and sum and 1 from operand to result, so dout, output_data_ready and every downstream h_fltr/steer_fltr register keep their cycle-by-cycle values.

Blocks and tiles: 24 blocks per h_fltr instance (4 each for f1, f2, h2; 3 each for f3, h1, h3, h4) times 6 h_fltr instances = 144 blocks, unchanged from the kept candidate. Each takes a DSP tile alone; the 42 fltr_compute instances keep their 57 tiles of mult_9x9_fixed_pt, so the design uses 201 tiles, as packing measured for the kept candidate at seed 1, against the baseline's 224.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block's bx is driven by another block, so the only block delay in the stage is 2.140 ns, against 5.450 ns of block-plus-wire in the kept candidate. The stage this rewrite leaves, using the seed-1 numbers from the kept candidate's own report for the same elements: 0.103 (clock to tap-register output) + 0.792 wire + 0.474 seventeen-stage pair-sum carry chain = 1.369; + 1.001 register-to-block wire + 2.140 block = 4.510; + 0.544 block-into-soft-logic wire + 0.778 twenty-eight-stage adder = 5.832; + 0.960 wire + 0.778 second adder level = 7.570; + 1.807 wire + 0.153 enable LUT = 9.530, plus 0.019 setup. The corr side path is 0.103 + 0.960 wire + 0.153 LUT = 1.216, + 1.001 wire = 2.217 at mul_a's bx, which is earlier than ax at 2.370, so the correction is off the critical path. The 7-tap mul_d side path is 0.103 + 1.419 register-to-block wire + 2.140 = 3.662, also slack. So the rewrite's stage is about 9.6 ns against the baseline's slowest stage of 11.6069 ns and its second slowest of 11.293 ns — and both of those stages are inside converted modules (my_fir_f1 and my_fir_f2), so they no longer exist. The slowest stage left outside the converted modules is fltr_compute's d_out_tmp sum: registered 9x9 products into six 20-bit adder levels, about 0.1 + 6x1.069 + a last wire, roughly 7.5-8.5 ns, below this stage; steer_fltr's deepest stage (im_p_tmp, lines 641/643) is four 31-bit terms, three adder levels, about 4 ns. So 9.6 ns is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves.

Soft logic leaving the stage: in each my_fir instance the six (or five) 28-bit adder levels of the original reduction go away, replaced by three 17-bit pair adders, nine corr LUTs and two 28-bit adder levels; seven (or six) hard multiplies become four (or three) blocks. That stage was the baseline's slowest and second slowest, so the removal is where the period comes from; the added soft adder level relative to the kept candidate is paid for by removing a block and a block-to-block wire from the same stage.

Candidates left, with reasons:

  • All 46 fltr_compute candidate rows (fltr_compute_f1 lines 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071), each 6 instances, are left. Three reasons, all of them sufficient. (a) Tiles: they are 8-bit by constant products packed four to a mult_9x9_fixed_pt tile, 294 products on 57 tiles; a block takes a tile alone, so converting even one module's seven products would cost about 5 extra tiles per instance, and converting all of them would need hundreds of tiles against a 306-tile device. (b) Their products are registered one stage before the sum (q1..q7, line 867 and its counterparts), so the block's adder cannot absorb the d_out_tmp reduction without deleting those registers and moving the whole 7-term sum into the multiply stage, which lengthens that stage and changes nothing on the critical path. (c) Their stage is roughly 7.5-8.5 ns, well under the slowest stage, so nothing bought there helps the period while every block added costs a tile (about 9 CLBs).
  • No my_fir candidate is left: all 46 rows across the seven modules are converted.

1	// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
6	// reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_mult_add_16 (
8	    input  [15:0] ax,
9	    input  [15:0] ay,
10	    input  [31:0] bx,
11	    output [63:0] result
12	);
13	
14	    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
15	    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact
16	
17	    assign result = sum;
18	
19	endmodule

PLAN:

This is a revision of the kept candidate. It keeps the same 144 blocks and the same symmetric folding, and changes two things that cost it 2.9 ns of carry chain in front of the blocks and 2.1 ns + 1.17 ns of block-to-block wire inside the stage:

  1. The carry correction is removed from the critical path by halving instead of truncating. The kept candidate fed ax = s[15:0] and had to add back the dropped bit 16 with corr = (s06[16]?c0:0)+(s15[16]?c1:0)+(s24[16]?c2:0), whose three terms depend on the carry out of the 17-bit pair adder: the seed-1 report shows that as $add~226 (5 stages) + $add~227 (1 stage) with their wires, 2.962 ns between the pair sum and the first block. Instead feed ax = s[16:1] (the full 17-bit sum shifted right by one, no bits lost) and ay = 2*c. Then ax*ay = (s>>1)*2c = s*c - s[0]*c, and the only missing term is s[0]*c, where s[0] = x[0]^y[0] is one XOR of two tap-register bits — it does not wait on the carry chain. The three missing terms are summed into one 9-bit corr written as a case over the three bits {p0,p1,p2} with constant arms, so each corr bit is a 3-input function, one LUT level, not an adder; corr is placed in mul_a's otherwise-unused bx. corr <= c0+c1+c2 <= 237 for every module, so it fits in 9 bits.
  2. The two block-to-block chains are broken. The kept candidate chained mul_a→mul_b and mul_c→mul_d through bx, putting two blocks plus a 1.17 ns block-to-block wire in one stage (2.140+1.170+2.140 = 5.45 ns). Here all four blocks run in parallel with bx tied to 0 (or to corr on mul_a) and their results are summed in a two-level soft adder tree of 28-bit adds. That trades 2 extra adders per 7-tap instance and 1 per 6-tap instance (60 extra 28-bit adds, about 1680 BLEs, roughly +5% used logic area) for 1.57 ns off the stage, about -14% on the period; the product moves in our favour because the baseline's two slowest stages both live in these modules, so no other stage holds the period up near 11 ns.

Correctness of the arithmetic, per module. The seven coefficient sets are symmetric (COEF0=COEF6, COEF1=COEF5, COEF2=COEF4; lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), so din*c0 + n_delay_reg6*c6 = s06*c0 and likewise for the other two pairs; COEF3 is 0 in f3/h1/h3/h4 and those sums have only six products, which is why those modules get three blocks and no mul_d. Summing the four (three) block results:
r_a + r_b + r_c (+ r_d) = s06*c0 + s15*c1 + s24*c2 (+ n_delay_reg3*c3) - (p0*c0 + p1*c1 + p2*c2) + corr, and corr is exactly that subtracted amount, so the total is the original sum term for term. All operands are unsigned and no value wraps: ax <= 65535, ay = 2*c <= 510 (both inside their 16-bit ports), each result <= 65535*510 + 237 < 2^26 (inside bx's 32 bits where it is reused, and far inside result's 64 bits), and the full sum is at most 65535*673 = 44.1e6 < 2^28, so the original 28-bit dout never truncated and the [27:0] slices of the block results lose nothing. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line: the halving identity holds for every 16-bit din, including the one module (my_fir_f3, fed from fltr_compute_f3 whose coefficient sum 1126*255 = 287130 can set bit 18 of d_out_tmp, line 936-937) whose din really can have bit 15 set.

Everything else in the my_fir modules is untouched: the tap shift register, the new_data_rdy enable on dout and on the taps, output_data_ready, and the else branch. The blocks are combinational and sit entirely inside the existing register-to-register stage, so no register is added, moved or removed, and no value that leaves the module goes inside a block — the only readers of the products are the dout sum itself (lines 1486-1492 and the matching lines in the other six modules), and the taps keep their own wires for the shift register.

Register stages, per converted region, before and after: before, each product is combinational from the tap registers (or din, itself a register output in h_fltr's source) into the same-cycle adder chain and lands in dout — 0 register stages between product and sum, 1 register stage from operand to result. After, the operand registers feed a 17-bit pair adder, one block, two soft adder levels and dout — still 0 register stages between product and sum and 1 from operand to result, so dout, output_data_ready and every downstream h_fltr/steer_fltr register keep their cycle-by-cycle values.

Blocks and tiles: 24 blocks per h_fltr instance (4 each for f1, f2, h2; 3 each for f3, h1, h3, h4) times 6 h_fltr instances = 144 blocks, unchanged from the kept candidate. Each takes a DSP tile alone; the 42 fltr_compute instances keep their 57 tiles of mult_9x9_fixed_pt, so the design uses 201 tiles, as packing measured for the kept candidate at seed 1, against the baseline's 224.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block's bx is driven by another block, so the only block delay in the stage is 2.140 ns, against 5.450 ns of block-plus-wire in the kept candidate. The stage this rewrite leaves, using the seed-1 numbers from the kept candidate's own report for the same elements: 0.103 (clock to tap-register output) + 0.792 wire + 0.474 seventeen-stage pair-sum carry chain = 1.369; + 1.001 register-to-block wire + 2.140 block = 4.510; + 0.544 block-into-soft-logic wire + 0.778 twenty-eight-stage adder = 5.832; + 0.960 wire + 0.778 second adder level = 7.570; + 1.807 wire + 0.153 enable LUT = 9.530, plus 0.019 setup. The corr side path is 0.103 + 0.960 wire + 0.153 LUT = 1.216, + 1.001 wire = 2.217 at mul_a's bx, which is earlier than ax at 2.370, so the correction is off the critical path. The 7-tap mul_d side path is 0.103 + 1.419 register-to-block wire + 2.140 = 3.662, also slack. So the rewrite's stage is about 9.6 ns against the baseline's slowest stage of 11.6069 ns and its second slowest of 11.293 ns — and both of those stages are inside converted modules (my_fir_f1 and my_fir_f2), so they no longer exist. The slowest stage left outside the converted modules is fltr_compute's d_out_tmp sum: registered 9x9 products into six 20-bit adder levels, about 0.1 + 6x1.069 + a last wire, roughly 7.5-8.5 ns, below this stage; steer_fltr's deepest stage (im_p_tmp, lines 641/643) is four 31-bit terms, three adder levels, about 4 ns. So 9.6 ns is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves.

Soft logic leaving the stage: in each my_fir instance the six (or five) 28-bit adder levels of the original reduction go away, replaced by three 17-bit pair adders, nine corr LUTs and two 28-bit adder levels; seven (or six) hard multiplies become four (or three) blocks. That stage was the baseline's slowest and second slowest, so the removal is where the period comes from; the added soft adder level relative to the kept candidate is paid for by removing a block and a block-to-block wire from the same stage.

Candidates left, with reasons:

  • All 46 fltr_compute candidate rows (fltr_compute_f1 lines 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071), each 6 instances, are left. Three reasons, all of them sufficient. (a) Tiles: they are 8-bit by constant products packed four to a mult_9x9_fixed_pt tile, 294 products on 57 tiles; a block takes a tile alone, so converting even one module's seven products would cost about 5 extra tiles per instance, and converting all of them would need hundreds of tiles against a 306-tile device. (b) Their products are registered one stage before the sum (q1..q7, line 867 and its counterparts), so the block's adder cannot absorb the d_out_tmp reduction without deleting those registers and moving the whole 7-term sum into the multiply stage, which lengthens that stage and changes nothing on the critical path. (c) Their stage is roughly 7.5-8.5 ns, well under the slowest stage, so nothing bought there helps the period while every block added costs a tile (about 9 CLBs).
  • No my_fir candidate is left: all 46 rows across the seven modules are converted.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

module my_fir_f1 (clk, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready, din, dout);

//coefdata=29,101,-15,-235,-15,101,29;

	//parameter `WIDTH = 5'b10000;

    input clk; 
    input[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] din; 
    output[28 - 1:0] dout; 
    reg[28 - 1:0] dout;
	input new_data_rdy;
	output output_data_ready;
	reg output_data_ready;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;


    wire p0 = din[0] ^ n_delay_reg6[0];
    wire p1 = n_delay_reg1[0] ^ n_delay_reg5[0];
    wire p2 = n_delay_reg2[0] ^ n_delay_reg4[0];

    wire[16:0] s06 = {1'b0, din} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg6};
    wire[16:0] s15 = {1'b0, n_delay_reg1} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg5};
    wire[16:0] s24 = {1'b0, n_delay_reg2} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg4};

    wire[15:0] coef0_x2 = 2 * `COEF0_b;
    wire[15:0] coef1_x2 = 2 * `COEF1_b;
    wire[15:0] coef2_x2 = 2 * `COEF2_b;
    wire[15:0] coef3_x1 = `COEF3_b;

    reg[8:0] corr;
    always @(*)
    begin
        case ({p0, p1, p2})
            3'b000: corr = 9'b0;
            3'b001: corr = `COEF2_b;
            3'b010: corr = `COEF1_b;
            3'b011: corr = `COEF1_b + `COEF2_b;
            3'b100: corr = `COEF0_b;
            3'b101: corr = `COEF0_b + `COEF2_b;
            3'b110: corr = `COEF0_b + `COEF1_b;
            3'b111: corr = `COEF0_b + `COEF1_b + `COEF2_b;
        endcase
    end

    wire[63:0] r_a;
    wire[63:0] r_b;
    wire[63:0] r_c;
    wire[63:0] r_d;

    comb_mult_add_16 mul_a (.ax(s06[16:1]), .ay(coef0_x2), .bx({23'b0, corr}), .result(r_a));
    comb_mult_add_16 mul_b (.ax(s15[16:1]), .ay(coef1_x2), .bx(32'b0), .result(r_b));
    comb_mult_add_16 mul_c (.ax(s24[16:1]), .ay(coef2_x2), .bx(32'b0), .result(r_c));
    comb_mult_add_16 mul_d (.ax(n_delay_reg3), .ay(coef3_x1), .bx(32'b0), .result(r_d));

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)
		begin
			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;
			n_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;
			n_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;
			n_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;
		
			output_data_ready <= 1'b1;
			dout <= (r_a[27:0] + r_b[27:0]) + (r_c[27:0] + r_d[27:0]);
		end
		else
		begin
			output_data_ready <= 1'b0;
		end
	end
endmodule

Task

You are the acceptance reviewer. You did not plan or write this edit. Check the edit against the approved plan, the block's contract and the correctness rules.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_mult_add_16 (precision INT16)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx
  • input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The design

The file stereovision2.v is the edited design. The edit is the diff below, taken against the original source.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.

  • Every block input port is connected, and the block's outputs drive what the plan says they drive.
  • The correctness rules hold for the edited source.

The synthesis checks and the reference simulation have passed; the remaining checks run after your review.

MAPPING: per my_fir instance, with p0 = din[0]^n_delay_reg6[0], p1 = n_delay_reg1[0]^n_delay_reg5[0], p2 = n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0], 17-bit pair sums s06={1'b0,din}+{1'b0,n_delay_reg6}, s15={1'b0,n_delay_reg1}+{1'b0,n_delay_reg5}, s24={1'b0,n_delay_reg2}+{1'b0,n_delay_reg4}, and a one-LUT-level constant select corr = p0*c0 + p1*c1 + p2*c2 (case over {p0,p1,p2}, 9 bits): mul_a .ax(s06[16:1]) .ay(c0<<1) .bx({23'b0,corr}) .result(r_a); mul_b .ax(s15[16:1]) .ay(c1<<1) .bx(32'b0) .result(r_b); mul_c .ax(s24[16:1]) .ay(c2<<1) .bx(32'b0) .result(r_c); and, in the three 7-tap modules only, mul_d .ax(n_delay_reg3) .ay(c3) .bx(32'b0) .result(r_d). Output: 7-tap dout <= (r_a[27:0] + r_b[27:0]) + (r_c[27:0] + r_d[27:0]), 6-tap dout <= (r_a[27:0] + r_b[27:0]) + r_c[27:0]. c0/c1/c2/c3 are the module's own macros: f1 COEF0_b,COEF1_b,COEF2_b,COEF3_b (29,101,15,235); f2 COEF0_c,COEF1_c,COEF2_c,COEF3_c (4,42,163,255); f3 COEF0_d,COEF1_d,COEF2_d (12,77,148); h1 COEF0_1,COEF1_1,COEF2_1 (15,25,193); h2 COEF0_2,COEF1_2,COEF2_2,COEF3_2 (4,42,163,255); h3 COEF0_3,COEF1_3,COEF2_3 (9,56,109); h4 COEF0_4,COEF1_4,COEF2_4 (9,56,109).
PLAN:

This is a revision of the kept candidate. It keeps the same 144 blocks and the same symmetric folding, and changes two things that cost it 2.9 ns of carry chain in front of the blocks and 2.1 ns + 1.17 ns of block-to-block wire inside the stage:

  1. The carry correction is removed from the critical path by halving instead of truncating. The kept candidate fed ax = s[15:0] and had to add back the dropped bit 16 with corr = (s06[16]?c0:0)+(s15[16]?c1:0)+(s24[16]?c2:0), whose three terms depend on the carry out of the 17-bit pair adder: the seed-1 report shows that as $add~226 (5 stages) + $add~227 (1 stage) with their wires, 2.962 ns between the pair sum and the first block. Instead feed ax = s[16:1] (the full 17-bit sum shifted right by one, no bits lost) and ay = 2*c. Then ax*ay = (s>>1)*2c = s*c - s[0]*c, and the only missing term is s[0]*c, where s[0] = x[0]^y[0] is one XOR of two tap-register bits — it does not wait on the carry chain. The three missing terms are summed into one 9-bit corr written as a case over the three bits {p0,p1,p2} with constant arms, so each corr bit is a 3-input function, one LUT level, not an adder; corr is placed in mul_a's otherwise-unused bx. corr <= c0+c1+c2 <= 237 for every module, so it fits in 9 bits.
  2. The two block-to-block chains are broken. The kept candidate chained mul_a→mul_b and mul_c→mul_d through bx, putting two blocks plus a 1.17 ns block-to-block wire in one stage (2.140+1.170+2.140 = 5.45 ns). Here all four blocks run in parallel with bx tied to 0 (or to corr on mul_a) and their results are summed in a two-level soft adder tree of 28-bit adds. That trades 2 extra adders per 7-tap instance and 1 per 6-tap instance (60 extra 28-bit adds, about 1680 BLEs, roughly +5% used logic area) for 1.57 ns off the stage, about -14% on the period; the product moves in our favour because the baseline's two slowest stages both live in these modules, so no other stage holds the period up near 11 ns.

Correctness of the arithmetic, per module. The seven coefficient sets are symmetric (COEF0=COEF6, COEF1=COEF5, COEF2=COEF4; lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), so din*c0 + n_delay_reg6*c6 = s06*c0 and likewise for the other two pairs; COEF3 is 0 in f3/h1/h3/h4 and those sums have only six products, which is why those modules get three blocks and no mul_d. Summing the four (three) block results:
r_a + r_b + r_c (+ r_d) = s06*c0 + s15*c1 + s24*c2 (+ n_delay_reg3*c3) - (p0*c0 + p1*c1 + p2*c2) + corr, and corr is exactly that subtracted amount, so the total is the original sum term for term. All operands are unsigned and no value wraps: ax <= 65535, ay = 2*c <= 510 (both inside their 16-bit ports), each result <= 65535*510 + 237 < 2^26 (inside bx's 32 bits where it is reused, and far inside result's 64 bits), and the full sum is at most 65535*673 = 44.1e6 < 2^28, so the original 28-bit dout never truncated and the [27:0] slices of the block results lose nothing. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line: the halving identity holds for every 16-bit din, including the one module (my_fir_f3, fed from fltr_compute_f3 whose coefficient sum 1126*255 = 287130 can set bit 18 of d_out_tmp, line 936-937) whose din really can have bit 15 set.

Everything else in the my_fir modules is untouched: the tap shift register, the new_data_rdy enable on dout and on the taps, output_data_ready, and the else branch. The blocks are combinational and sit entirely inside the existing register-to-register stage, so no register is added, moved or removed, and no value that leaves the module goes inside a block — the only readers of the products are the dout sum itself (lines 1486-1492 and the matching lines in the other six modules), and the taps keep their own wires for the shift register.

Register stages, per converted region, before and after: before, each product is combinational from the tap registers (or din, itself a register output in h_fltr's source) into the same-cycle adder chain and lands in dout — 0 register stages between product and sum, 1 register stage from operand to result. After, the operand registers feed a 17-bit pair adder, one block, two soft adder levels and dout — still 0 register stages between product and sum and 1 from operand to result, so dout, output_data_ready and every downstream h_fltr/steer_fltr register keep their cycle-by-cycle values.

Blocks and tiles: 24 blocks per h_fltr instance (4 each for f1, f2, h2; 3 each for f3, h1, h3, h4) times 6 h_fltr instances = 144 blocks, unchanged from the kept candidate. Each takes a DSP tile alone; the 42 fltr_compute instances keep their 57 tiles of mult_9x9_fixed_pt, so the design uses 201 tiles, as packing measured for the kept candidate at seed 1, against the baseline's 224.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. No block's bx is driven by another block, so the only block delay in the stage is 2.140 ns, against 5.450 ns of block-plus-wire in the kept candidate. The stage this rewrite leaves, using the seed-1 numbers from the kept candidate's own report for the same elements: 0.103 (clock to tap-register output) + 0.792 wire + 0.474 seventeen-stage pair-sum carry chain = 1.369; + 1.001 register-to-block wire + 2.140 block = 4.510; + 0.544 block-into-soft-logic wire + 0.778 twenty-eight-stage adder = 5.832; + 0.960 wire + 0.778 second adder level = 7.570; + 1.807 wire + 0.153 enable LUT = 9.530, plus 0.019 setup. The corr side path is 0.103 + 0.960 wire + 0.153 LUT = 1.216, + 1.001 wire = 2.217 at mul_a's bx, which is earlier than ax at 2.370, so the correction is off the critical path. The 7-tap mul_d side path is 0.103 + 1.419 register-to-block wire + 2.140 = 3.662, also slack. So the rewrite's stage is about 9.6 ns against the baseline's slowest stage of 11.6069 ns and its second slowest of 11.293 ns — and both of those stages are inside converted modules (my_fir_f1 and my_fir_f2), so they no longer exist. The slowest stage left outside the converted modules is fltr_compute's d_out_tmp sum: registered 9x9 products into six 20-bit adder levels, about 0.1 + 6x1.069 + a last wire, roughly 7.5-8.5 ns, below this stage; steer_fltr's deepest stage (im_p_tmp, lines 641/643) is four 31-bit terms, three adder levels, about 4 ns. So 9.6 ns is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves.

Soft logic leaving the stage: in each my_fir instance the six (or five) 28-bit adder levels of the original reduction go away, replaced by three 17-bit pair adders, nine corr LUTs and two 28-bit adder levels; seven (or six) hard multiplies become four (or three) blocks. That stage was the baseline's slowest and second slowest, so the removal is where the period comes from; the added soft adder level relative to the kept candidate is paid for by removing a block and a block-to-block wire from the same stage.

Candidates left, with reasons:

  • All 46 fltr_compute candidate rows (fltr_compute_f1 lines 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071), each 6 instances, are left. Three reasons, all of them sufficient. (a) Tiles: they are 8-bit by constant products packed four to a mult_9x9_fixed_pt tile, 294 products on 57 tiles; a block takes a tile alone, so converting even one module's seven products would cost about 5 extra tiles per instance, and converting all of them would need hundreds of tiles against a 306-tile device. (b) Their products are registered one stage before the sum (q1..q7, line 867 and its counterparts), so the block's adder cannot absorb the d_out_tmp reduction without deleting those registers and moving the whole 7-term sum into the multiply stage, which lengthens that stage and changes nothing on the critical path. (c) Their stage is roughly 7.5-8.5 ns, well under the slowest stage, so nothing bought there helps the period while every block added costs a tile (about 9 CLBs).
  • No my_fir candidate is left: all 46 rows across the seven modules are converted.

No other module (fltr_compute_*, h_fltr, steer_fltr, v_fltr_*, fifo*, port_bus_2to1) is touched.

  • Terms. Symmetry holds in every coefficient set (f1 29/101/15, f2 & h2 4/42/163, f3 12/77/148, h1 15/25/193, h3 & h4 9/56/109; lines 1440-1449, 1533-1539, 1627-1633, 1713-1722, 1803-1809, 1895-1901, 1984-1990), so pair folding keeps each term. COEF3 is nonzero only in f1/f2/h2, which are the three modules given mul_d; the four modules whose source sum has only six products get three blocks and no mul_d. The halving identity s*c = (s>>1)*2c + s[0]*c with s[0] = x[0]^y[0] is exact, and corr (case over {p0,p1,p2}) reproduces the three missing terms in mul_a.bx.

  • Registers / reset. No register added, moved or removed: corr is a full-case combinational reg (all eight arms assigned, no latch), the blocks are combinational, and the tap shift register, new_data_rdy gating, output_data_ready and the else branch are unchanged, so cycle-by-cycle behavior and post-reset behavior are preserved for any register start state.
  • Visibility. Nothing that leaves the module was moved inside a block; the only readers of the former products were the dout sums.
  • No ASSUMES line is needed, and none is claimed; the rewrite is unconditional on the input data.

1	// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
6	// reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_mult_add_16 (
8	    input  [15:0] ax,
9	    input  [15:0] ay,
10	    input  [31:0] bx,
11	    output [63:0] result
12	);
13	
14	    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
15	    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact
16	
17	    assign result = sum;
18	
19	endmodule

  • primitive to instantiate: comb_mult_add_16 (precision INT16)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx
  • input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • The block's internal delay is fixed. Soft logic between a block's output and the next register adds to that stage; blocks in series each add their delay plus a wire.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.

PLAN:

Why this differs from the kept candidate (revision 1). Revision 1 put all three symmetric pair products plus the centre tap of every my_fir into blocks (144 blocks, 206 tiles). The seed-1 path it leaves is reg -> pair adder -> block -> adder -> adder -> LUT -> dffe = 9.354 ns, of which the block hop alone is 1.314 (wire) + 2.140 (block) = 3.45 ns. Every coefficient in these filters is a small constant (4, 9, 12, 15, 25, 29, 42, 56, 77, 101, 109, 148, 163, 193, 235, 255), and each has a shift/add form of depth at most 2, i.e. two soft adder levels, which on this design is about 2.1-3.2 ns — no slower than the single block hop it replaces, and far cheaper: a block takes a whole DSP tile (253779, about 9 CLBs), while two 28-bit carry-chain adders cost roughly a fifth of that. So blocks are kept only where they buy the most (one per instance, on the tap whose constant needs the deepest/widest shift-add tree), and the remaining taps of the same sum are computed outside the block. That trades 102 DSP tiles (-2.6e7 area) for about 22 extra soft adders per h_fltr instance (+5e6 area), with the stage delay unchanged.

Rewrite, per my_fir module (applied to the unmodified source; all six instances of each module inherit it). Insert before the existing always block, and replace only the dout <= ... expression inside it. All intermediates are 28-bit wires built by explicit zero-extension from the 17-bit pair sums, so every value is exact and the low 28 bits assigned to dout match the original dout exactly (the true sum is at most about 4.4e7 < 2^28, so no wrap occurs in either version; the shift/add forms are congruent mod 2^28 regardless).

  • Common to all seven: wire[16:0] s06, s15, s24 as above; wire[27:0] x0={11'b0,s06}, x1={11'b0,s15}, x2={11'b0,s24}; wire[63:0] r.
  • my_fir_f1 (29,101,15,235): block on the centre tap n_delay_reg3*235. Outside: t0a=(x0<<1)+x0; T0=(x0<<5)-t0a (=29*s06), t1a=(x1<<1)+x1; t1b=(x1<<2)+x1; T1=(t1a<<5)+t1b (=101*s15), T2=(x2<<4)-x2 (=15*s24), T3=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+(T2+T3);
  • my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (4,42,163,255): block on s24*163. Outside: T0=x0<<2 (=4*s06, no adder), t1a=(x1<<2)+x1; t1b=(x1<<4)+t1a; T1=t1b<<1 (=42*s15), T2=r[27:0], x3={12'b0,n_delay_reg3}; T3=(x3<<8)-x3 (=255*n_delay_reg3). dout <= (T0+T1)+(T2+T3);
  • my_fir_f3 (12,77,148): block on s15*77. Outside: T0=(x0<<3)+(x0<<2) (=12*s06), T1=r[27:0], t2a=(x2<<2)+x2; t2b=(x2<<5)+t2a; T2=t2b<<2 (=148*s24). dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;
  • my_fir_h1 (15,25,193): block on s24*193. Outside: T0=(x0<<4)-x0 (=15*s06), t1a=(x1<<5)-(x1<<3); T1=t1a+x1 (=25*s15), T2=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;
  • my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109): block on s24*109. Outside: T0=(x0<<3)+x0 (=9*s06), T1=(x1<<6)-(x1<<3) (=56*s15), T2=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;

Correctness. Each module's sum is symmetric (c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4), so din*c0+n6*c6 = s06*c0 and likewise for the other two pairs; the 6-tap modules (f3, h1, h3, h4) have c3=0 and omit n_delay_reg3 from the sum, which the rewrite keeps omitted (the register itself is still shifted, unchanged). For a pair fed to a block, s = 2*s[16:1] + s[0] and s[0] is the xor of the two addends' LSBs (there is no carry into bit 0), so ax*ay + bx = s[16:1]*2c + s[0]*c = s*c exactly; ax is 16 bits as required because the pair sum is 17 bits, and ay (154/218/326/386) and bx (at most 193) are well inside their ports. For my_fir_f1 the block takes the 16-bit register n_delay_reg3 directly with ay=235, so no split and no correction are needed and bx is tied to 0. The block is combinational, result is valid in the same cycle, and the result never approaches 2^64. Every subtraction written above has a non-negative true value (32x-3x, 16x-x, 256x-x, 64x-8x, 32x-8x). No signal that leaves the module is moved inside a block: din and the six n_delay_regs keep their own nets, output_data_ready and the new_data_rdy enable are untouched, and only dout's expression changes. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line.

Registers and reset. No register is moved, added or removed. For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result are 0 before the rewrite and 0 after: the products and the whole reduction are combinational between the n_delay_reg/din registers and the dout register, inside the same new_data_rdy-enabled stage, in both versions. Because nothing is added, there is no register whose unknown initial value could be relied on, and the enabled dout/output_data_ready behaviour after any reset is unchanged.

Blocks, tiles, and block series. The rewrite instantiates 42 blocks, one per my_fir instance (7 modules x 6 h_fltr instances). At seed 1 the kept candidate packed 206 tiles with 144 blocks, i.e. 62 tiles for everything else (the fltr_compute 9x9 products); with 42 blocks the design should use 42 + 62 = 104 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 206 in the kept candidate. No block feeds another block: the longest series of blocks in any stage is 1, costing 2.14 ns plus about 1.3 ns of wire into it, inside a stage budgeted at about 9.3 ns.

Stage delay. The stage the rewrite leaves is the same my_fir register-to-register stage that is critical today. Its two longest shapes are: through the block, reg -> pair adder (1.00 + 0.40) -> wire 1.31 -> block 2.14 -> sum-tree adder (0.96 + 0.32) -> sum-tree adder (1.42 + 0.39) -> wire 1.18 + LUT 0.15 = about 9.3 ns, identical to the measured 9.354 ns path since nothing was added to it; and through the deepest soft tap, reg -> pair adder -> two constant-multiply adder levels -> two sum-tree adder levels -> LUT = 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 soft levels, about 9.2 ns at the 1.6 ns/level seen on the current critical path and about 7.7 ns at the 1.069 ns median. So no stage gets longer than the stage that is already slowest, and the slowest stage is expected to stay at or just below 9.35 ns; the next stages in the design are unchanged and were all at or below 9.35 ns in the kept candidate.

What soft logic leaves which stage, relative to the unmodified design. From the my_fir stage (the slowest stage, 11.607 ns in the baseline) the rewrite removes the six-deep chain of 28-bit adders that summed 6 or 7 products: it becomes three 17-bit pair adders, at most two constant-multiply adder levels per tap, and a two-level sum tree of 3 or 4 terms, i.e. depth 6 becomes depth 5 with one hop replaced by the block. One hard multiply per instance moves into the block; the other 5 or 6 hard multiplies of that instance are replaced by shift/add trees of 0 to 3 adders each. No other stage of the design is touched.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • my_fir_f1 1486$154, 1487$155, 1488$157, 1490$161, 1491$163, 1492$165; my_fir_f2 1542$169, 1543$170, 1545$174, 1547$178, 1548$180; my_fir_f3 1602$184, 1604$187, 1605$189, 1607$193; my_fir_h1 1661$197, 1662$198, 1665$204, 1666$206; my_fir_h2 1716$210, 1717$211, 1719$215, 1721$219, 1722$221; my_fir_h3 1775$225, 1776$226, 1779$232, 1780$234; my_fir_h4 1833$238, 1834$239, 1837$245, 1838$247 — left out of the blocks, but regrouped with their symmetric partners into the pair sums and computed outside the block as explicit shift/add trees, because the block offers only one multiply per DSP tile: giving each of these a block would cost 253779 apiece (about 9 CLBs) while its constant needs at most three 28-bit adders, roughly a fifth of that area, and a depth-2 tree is no slower than the block's 1.31 + 2.14 ns hop. Keeping them in blocks is exactly what makes the kept candidate's area 8.95e7 instead of about 6.9e7.
  • All 46 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 859$44 to 865$50, f2 889$58 to 895$64, f3 928$72 to 934$78, h1 959$86 to 965$92, h2 992$100 to 998$106, h3 1030$114 to 1036$120, h4 1065$128 to 1071$134) — left exactly as they are. They are 8-bit by 9-bit products that already pack four to a DSP tile on 39 tiles; one block each would need 7 tiles per instance (about 270 tiles overall, more than the device holds alongside the my_fir blocks) for products that are not on the critical path, since the products are registered in q1..q7 one stage before their sum and that sum stage was below both of the baseline's two slowest stages and below the 9.35 ns the rewritten my_fir leaves. Any block here would be paid for at about 9 CLBs and shorten nothing.

Expected effect on the objective. Against the kept candidate: 102 fewer DSP tiles (-2.59e7 area) against roughly 22 extra soft adders per h_fltr instance (+5e6), so about 6.9e7 used logic area (A/A0 about 0.70); period held at or just under 9.35 ns (D/D0 about 0.81); wirelength should fall further, since the removed blocks each routed a wide result out of a DSP tile and the replacements are local carry chains with hard-wired shifts. That puts the product near 0.50 of baseline against the kept candidate's 0.652. Even if the soft trees cost a full extra adder level and the period rose to 10.5 ns, the product would still be about 0.56, below the kept candidate.

DESIGN_CHANGE: each my_fir's din is a fltr_compute output d_out_tmp[18:3], whose value is bounded by the 8-bit pixel input times the filter's coefficient sum (at most 21451 for the modules feeding my_fir_f1/f2/h1/h2/h3/h4), so for all but my_fir_f3 the 17-bit pair sum would fit in 16 bits. If the design declared that bound (or narrowed those douts), the block could take the pair sum directly on ax with ay the plain coefficient, dropping the [16:1] split and the bx correction term entirely.
