Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

The plan

I'll read the source and the current state before planning a revision.

TIER: T2
REGIONS: my_fir_f1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1489$159, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1544$172, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1546$176, my_fir_f3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1603$185, my_fir_f3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1606$191, my_fir_h1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1663$200, my_fir_h1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1664$202, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1718$213, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1720$217, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1777$228, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1778$230, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1835$241, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1836$243
SHARED_REDUCTION: the dout sum of each my_fir module — seven reductions, one per module (my_fir_f1 1486-1492, my_fir_f2 1542-1548, my_fir_f3 1602-1607, my_fir_h1 1661-1666, my_fir_h2 1716-1722, my_fir_h3 1775-1780, my_fir_h4 1833-1838), each instantiated 6 times through h_fltr (lines 188-190, 195-197, 514-520)
BLOCKS: 42
TILES: 104
STAGE_NS: 9.3
MAPPING: one block per my_fir instance, on that module's costliest-coefficient tap; every other tap of the same dout sum is computed outside the block as an explicit shift/add tree. Pair sums (17 bit) s06={1'b0,din}+{1'b0,n_delay_reg6}, s15={1'b0,n_delay_reg1}+{1'b0,n_delay_reg5}, s24={1'b0,n_delay_reg2}+{1'b0,n_delay_reg4}. my_fir_f1: .ax(n_delay_reg3) .ay(16'd235) .bx(32'b0) .result(r) — the centre tap needs no pair sum and no correction. my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2: .ax(s24[16:1]) .ay(16'd326) .bx({23'b0, (n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) ? 9'd163 : 9'd0}) .result(r). my_fir_f3: .ax(s15[16:1]) .ay(16'd154) .bx({23'b0, (n_delay_reg1[0]^n_delay_reg5[0]) ? 9'd77 : 9'd0}) .result(r). my_fir_h1: .ax(s24[16:1]) .ay(16'd386) .bx({23'b0, (n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) ? 9'd193 : 9'd0}) .result(r). my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4: .ax(s24[16:1]) .ay(16'd218) .bx({23'b0, (n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) ? 9'd109 : 9'd0}) .result(r). In every case the block's result[27:0] is one term of the module's dout sum.
PLAN:

Why this differs from the kept candidate (revision 1). Revision 1 put all three symmetric pair products plus the centre tap of every my_fir into blocks (144 blocks, 206 tiles). The seed-1 path it leaves is reg -> pair adder -> block -> adder -> adder -> LUT -> dffe = 9.354 ns, of which the block hop alone is 1.314 (wire) + 2.140 (block) = 3.45 ns. Every coefficient in these filters is a small constant (4, 9, 12, 15, 25, 29, 42, 56, 77, 101, 109, 148, 163, 193, 235, 255), and each has a shift/add form of depth at most 2, i.e. two soft adder levels, which on this design is about 2.1-3.2 ns — no slower than the single block hop it replaces, and far cheaper: a block takes a whole DSP tile (253779, about 9 CLBs), while two 28-bit carry-chain adders cost roughly a fifth of that. So blocks are kept only where they buy the most (one per instance, on the tap whose constant needs the deepest/widest shift-add tree), and the remaining taps of the same sum are computed outside the block. That trades 102 DSP tiles (-2.6e7 area) for about 22 extra soft adders per h_fltr instance (+5e6 area), with the stage delay unchanged.

Rewrite, per my_fir module (applied to the unmodified source; all six instances of each module inherit it). Insert before the existing always block, and replace only the dout <= ... expression inside it. All intermediates are 28-bit wires built by explicit zero-extension from the 17-bit pair sums, so every value is exact and the low 28 bits assigned to dout match the original dout exactly (the true sum is at most about 4.4e7 < 2^28, so no wrap occurs in either version; the shift/add forms are congruent mod 2^28 regardless).

  • Common to all seven: wire[16:0] s06, s15, s24 as above; wire[27:0] x0={11'b0,s06}, x1={11'b0,s15}, x2={11'b0,s24}; wire[63:0] r.
  • my_fir_f1 (29,101,15,235): block on the centre tap n_delay_reg3*235. Outside: t0a=(x0<<1)+x0; T0=(x0<<5)-t0a (=29*s06), t1a=(x1<<1)+x1; t1b=(x1<<2)+x1; T1=(t1a<<5)+t1b (=101*s15), T2=(x2<<4)-x2 (=15*s24), T3=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+(T2+T3);
  • my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (4,42,163,255): block on s24*163. Outside: T0=x0<<2 (=4*s06, no adder), t1a=(x1<<2)+x1; t1b=(x1<<4)+t1a; T1=t1b<<1 (=42*s15), T2=r[27:0], x3={12'b0,n_delay_reg3}; T3=(x3<<8)-x3 (=255*n_delay_reg3). dout <= (T0+T1)+(T2+T3);
  • my_fir_f3 (12,77,148): block on s15*77. Outside: T0=(x0<<3)+(x0<<2) (=12*s06), T1=r[27:0], t2a=(x2<<2)+x2; t2b=(x2<<5)+t2a; T2=t2b<<2 (=148*s24). dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;
  • my_fir_h1 (15,25,193): block on s24*193. Outside: T0=(x0<<4)-x0 (=15*s06), t1a=(x1<<5)-(x1<<3); T1=t1a+x1 (=25*s15), T2=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;
  • my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109): block on s24*109. Outside: T0=(x0<<3)+x0 (=9*s06), T1=(x1<<6)-(x1<<3) (=56*s15), T2=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;

Correctness. Each module's sum is symmetric (c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4), so din*c0+n6*c6 = s06*c0 and likewise for the other two pairs; the 6-tap modules (f3, h1, h3, h4) have c3=0 and omit n_delay_reg3 from the sum, which the rewrite keeps omitted (the register itself is still shifted, unchanged). For a pair fed to a block, s = 2*s[16:1] + s[0] and s[0] is the xor of the two addends' LSBs (there is no carry into bit 0), so ax*ay + bx = s[16:1]*2c + s[0]*c = s*c exactly; ax is 16 bits as required because the pair sum is 17 bits, and ay (154/218/326/386) and bx (at most 193) are well inside their ports. For my_fir_f1 the block takes the 16-bit register n_delay_reg3 directly with ay=235, so no split and no correction are needed and bx is tied to 0. The block is combinational, result is valid in the same cycle, and the result never approaches 2^64. Every subtraction written above has a non-negative true value (32x-3x, 16x-x, 256x-x, 64x-8x, 32x-8x). No signal that leaves the module is moved inside a block: din and the six n_delay_regs keep their own nets, output_data_ready and the new_data_rdy enable are untouched, and only dout's expression changes. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line.

Registers and reset. No register is moved, added or removed. For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result are 0 before the rewrite and 0 after: the products and the whole reduction are combinational between the n_delay_reg/din registers and the dout register, inside the same new_data_rdy-enabled stage, in both versions. Because nothing is added, there is no register whose unknown initial value could be relied on, and the enabled dout/output_data_ready behaviour after any reset is unchanged.

Blocks, tiles, and block series. The rewrite instantiates 42 blocks, one per my_fir instance (7 modules x 6 h_fltr instances). At seed 1 the kept candidate packed 206 tiles with 144 blocks, i.e. 62 tiles for everything else (the fltr_compute 9x9 products); with 42 blocks the design should use 42 + 62 = 104 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 206 in the kept candidate. No block feeds another block: the longest series of blocks in any stage is 1, costing 2.14 ns plus about 1.3 ns of wire into it, inside a stage budgeted at about 9.3 ns.

Stage delay. The stage the rewrite leaves is the same my_fir register-to-register stage that is critical today. Its two longest shapes are: through the block, reg -> pair adder (1.00 + 0.40) -> wire 1.31 -> block 2.14 -> sum-tree adder (0.96 + 0.32) -> sum-tree adder (1.42 + 0.39) -> wire 1.18 + LUT 0.15 = about 9.3 ns, identical to the measured 9.354 ns path since nothing was added to it; and through the deepest soft tap, reg -> pair adder -> two constant-multiply adder levels -> two sum-tree adder levels -> LUT = 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 soft levels, about 9.2 ns at the 1.6 ns/level seen on the current critical path and about 7.7 ns at the 1.069 ns median. So no stage gets longer than the stage that is already slowest, and the slowest stage is expected to stay at or just below 9.35 ns; the next stages in the design are unchanged and were all at or below 9.35 ns in the kept candidate.

What soft logic leaves which stage, relative to the unmodified design. From the my_fir stage (the slowest stage, 11.607 ns in the baseline) the rewrite removes the six-deep chain of 28-bit adders that summed 6 or 7 products: it becomes three 17-bit pair adders, at most two constant-multiply adder levels per tap, and a two-level sum tree of 3 or 4 terms, i.e. depth 6 becomes depth 5 with one hop replaced by the block. One hard multiply per instance moves into the block; the other 5 or 6 hard multiplies of that instance are replaced by shift/add trees of 0 to 3 adders each. No other stage of the design is touched.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • my_fir_f1 1486$154, 1487$155, 1488$157, 1490$161, 1491$163, 1492$165; my_fir_f2 1542$169, 1543$170, 1545$174, 1547$178, 1548$180; my_fir_f3 1602$184, 1604$187, 1605$189, 1607$193; my_fir_h1 1661$197, 1662$198, 1665$204, 1666$206; my_fir_h2 1716$210, 1717$211, 1719$215, 1721$219, 1722$221; my_fir_h3 1775$225, 1776$226, 1779$232, 1780$234; my_fir_h4 1833$238, 1834$239, 1837$245, 1838$247 — left out of the blocks, but regrouped with their symmetric partners into the pair sums and computed outside the block as explicit shift/add trees, because the block offers only one multiply per DSP tile: giving each of these a block would cost 253779 apiece (about 9 CLBs) while its constant needs at most three 28-bit adders, roughly a fifth of that area, and a depth-2 tree is no slower than the block's 1.31 + 2.14 ns hop. Keeping them in blocks is exactly what makes the kept candidate's area 8.95e7 instead of about 6.9e7.
  • All 46 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 859$44 to 865$50, f2 889$58 to 895$64, f3 928$72 to 934$78, h1 959$86 to 965$92, h2 992$100 to 998$106, h3 1030$114 to 1036$120, h4 1065$128 to 1071$134) — left exactly as they are. They are 8-bit by 9-bit products that already pack four to a DSP tile on 39 tiles; one block each would need 7 tiles per instance (about 270 tiles overall, more than the device holds alongside the my_fir blocks) for products that are not on the critical path, since the products are registered in q1..q7 one stage before their sum and that sum stage was below both of the baseline's two slowest stages and below the 9.35 ns the rewritten my_fir leaves. Any block here would be paid for at about 9 CLBs and shorten nothing.

Expected effect on the objective. Against the kept candidate: 102 fewer DSP tiles (-2.59e7 area) against roughly 22 extra soft adders per h_fltr instance (+5e6), so about 6.9e7 used logic area (A/A0 about 0.70); period held at or just under 9.35 ns (D/D0 about 0.81); wirelength should fall further, since the removed blocks each routed a wide result out of a DSP tile and the replacements are local carry chains with hard-wired shifts. That puts the product near 0.50 of baseline against the kept candidate's 0.652. Even if the soft trees cost a full extra adder level and the period rose to 10.5 ns, the product would still be about 0.56, below the kept candidate.

DESIGN_CHANGE: each my_fir's din is a fltr_compute output d_out_tmp[18:3], whose value is bounded by the 8-bit pixel input times the filter's coefficient sum (at most 21451 for the modules feeding my_fir_f1/f2/h1/h2/h3/h4), so for all but my_fir_f3 the 17-bit pair sum would fit in 16 bits. If the design declared that bound (or narrowed those douts), the block could take the pair sum directly on ax with ay the plain coefficient, dropping the [16:1] split and the bx correction term entirely.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_mult_add_16.v) are in sim_reference/.

Verified against stereovision2.v:

  • Coefficients and symmetry — f1 (29,101,15,235) lines 1440-1449, f2 (4,42,163,255) 1500-1506, f3 (12,77,148, c3=0) 1561-1567, h1 (15,25,193) 1616-1625, h2 1675-1681, h3 1734-1740, h4 1792-1798. All are symmetric (c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4), so the pair-sum regrouping is exact; the four 6-tap modules omit n_delay_reg3 (lines 1602-1607, 1661-1666, 1775-1780, 1833-1838) and the plan keeps it omitted while leaving the register's shift intact.
  • Block mapping — for a 17-bit pair sum s, s[0] is the xor of the two LSBs, so s[16:1]*2c + s[0]*c = s*c; ax is 16 bits, ay (154/218/326/386/235) and bx (≤193) fit their ports, every input port is named and the unused bx is tied to 0. Largest block result (386·65535+193 ≈ 2.5e7) and largest dout (673·65535 ≈ 4.4e7 for f2/h2) are both below 2^28, so r[27:0] and the 28-bit dout truncation match the original 32-bit unsigned expression exactly. All shift/add forms check out (29=32−3, 101=96+5, 15=16−1, 42=2(16+5), 255=256−1, 12=8+4, 148=4(32+5), 25=32−8+1, 9=8+1, 56=64−8), every subtraction is non-negative, and no shifted intermediate exceeds 28 bits.
  • Visibility/registers — din and n_delay_reg1..6 are read only inside their own module's dout expression; nothing that leaves the module moves into a block. No register is added, moved or removed; dout/output_data_ready keep the new_data_rdy enable, so post-reset behaviour is unchanged and no ASSUMES is needed.
  • Required items — all 45 my_fir candidates (13 converted, 32 left) and all 46 fltr_compute candidates are accounted for with reasons; 42 blocks (6 h_fltr instances at lines 188-190/195-197 × 7 my_fir at 514-520), 104 tiles, longest block series 1 at 2.14 ns plus ~1.3 ns wire in a ~9.3 ns stage, the soft logic leaving the my_fir stage (stated as the slowest), and 0 register stages operand-to-result before and after for each converted region.

One non-blocking note: the DESIGN_CHANGE bound on din is overstated — fltr_compute's d_out_tmp sums sign-extended 17-bit q terms (line 867 and its six twins), so d_out_tmp[18:3] (line 868) can reach near 2^16 and a pair sum can exceed 16 bits. The rewrite does not rely on that bound, so correctness is unaffected, but the suggested narrowing would not be safe as written.

1	// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
6	// reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_mult_add_16 (
8	    input  [15:0] ax,
9	    input  [15:0] ay,
10	    input  [31:0] bx,
11	    output [63:0] result
12	);
13	
14	    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
15	    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact
16	
17	    assign result = sum;
18	
19	endmodule

Task

Edit stereovision2.v in this directory to carry out the approved plan below: rewrite the regions it names onto the hard block described next. If a step cannot be done as the plan says, stop and say which step and why; do not improvise a different rewrite.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_mult_add_16 (precision INT16)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx
  • input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The design
  • Regions in the approved plan: my_fir_f1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1489$159, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1544$172, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1546$176, my_fir_f3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1603$185, my_fir_f3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1606$191, my_fir_h1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1663$200, my_fir_h1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1664$202, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1718$213, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1720$217, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1777$228, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1778$230, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1835$241, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1836$243. The plan names their shared sum as 'the dout sum of each my_fir module — seven reductions, one per module (my_fir_f1 1486-1492, my_fir_f2 1542-1548, my_fir_f3 1602-1607, my_fir_h1 1661-1666, my_fir_h2 1716-1722, my_fir_h3 1775-1780, my_fir_h4 1833-1838), each instantiated 6 times through h_fltr (lines 188-190, 195-197, 514-520)'. Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.

PLAN:

Why this differs from the kept candidate (revision 1). Revision 1 put all three symmetric pair products plus the centre tap of every my_fir into blocks (144 blocks, 206 tiles). The seed-1 path it leaves is reg -> pair adder -> block -> adder -> adder -> LUT -> dffe = 9.354 ns, of which the block hop alone is 1.314 (wire) + 2.140 (block) = 3.45 ns. Every coefficient in these filters is a small constant (4, 9, 12, 15, 25, 29, 42, 56, 77, 101, 109, 148, 163, 193, 235, 255), and each has a shift/add form of depth at most 2, i.e. two soft adder levels, which on this design is about 2.1-3.2 ns — no slower than the single block hop it replaces, and far cheaper: a block takes a whole DSP tile (253779, about 9 CLBs), while two 28-bit carry-chain adders cost roughly a fifth of that. So blocks are kept only where they buy the most (one per instance, on the tap whose constant needs the deepest/widest shift-add tree), and the remaining taps of the same sum are computed outside the block. That trades 102 DSP tiles (-2.6e7 area) for about 22 extra soft adders per h_fltr instance (+5e6 area), with the stage delay unchanged.

Rewrite, per my_fir module (applied to the unmodified source; all six instances of each module inherit it). Insert before the existing always block, and replace only the dout <= ... expression inside it. All intermediates are 28-bit wires built by explicit zero-extension from the 17-bit pair sums, so every value is exact and the low 28 bits assigned to dout match the original dout exactly (the true sum is at most about 4.4e7 < 2^28, so no wrap occurs in either version; the shift/add forms are congruent mod 2^28 regardless).

  • Common to all seven: wire[16:0] s06, s15, s24 as above; wire[27:0] x0={11'b0,s06}, x1={11'b0,s15}, x2={11'b0,s24}; wire[63:0] r.
  • my_fir_f1 (29,101,15,235): block on the centre tap n_delay_reg3*235. Outside: t0a=(x0<<1)+x0; T0=(x0<<5)-t0a (=29*s06), t1a=(x1<<1)+x1; t1b=(x1<<2)+x1; T1=(t1a<<5)+t1b (=101*s15), T2=(x2<<4)-x2 (=15*s24), T3=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+(T2+T3);
  • my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (4,42,163,255): block on s24*163. Outside: T0=x0<<2 (=4*s06, no adder), t1a=(x1<<2)+x1; t1b=(x1<<4)+t1a; T1=t1b<<1 (=42*s15), T2=r[27:0], x3={12'b0,n_delay_reg3}; T3=(x3<<8)-x3 (=255*n_delay_reg3). dout <= (T0+T1)+(T2+T3);
  • my_fir_f3 (12,77,148): block on s15*77. Outside: T0=(x0<<3)+(x0<<2) (=12*s06), T1=r[27:0], t2a=(x2<<2)+x2; t2b=(x2<<5)+t2a; T2=t2b<<2 (=148*s24). dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;
  • my_fir_h1 (15,25,193): block on s24*193. Outside: T0=(x0<<4)-x0 (=15*s06), t1a=(x1<<5)-(x1<<3); T1=t1a+x1 (=25*s15), T2=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;
  • my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109): block on s24*109. Outside: T0=(x0<<3)+x0 (=9*s06), T1=(x1<<6)-(x1<<3) (=56*s15), T2=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;

Correctness. Each module's sum is symmetric (c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4), so din*c0+n6*c6 = s06*c0 and likewise for the other two pairs; the 6-tap modules (f3, h1, h3, h4) have c3=0 and omit n_delay_reg3 from the sum, which the rewrite keeps omitted (the register itself is still shifted, unchanged). For a pair fed to a block, s = 2*s[16:1] + s[0] and s[0] is the xor of the two addends' LSBs (there is no carry into bit 0), so ax*ay + bx = s[16:1]*2c + s[0]*c = s*c exactly; ax is 16 bits as required because the pair sum is 17 bits, and ay (154/218/326/386) and bx (at most 193) are well inside their ports. For my_fir_f1 the block takes the 16-bit register n_delay_reg3 directly with ay=235, so no split and no correction are needed and bx is tied to 0. The block is combinational, result is valid in the same cycle, and the result never approaches 2^64. Every subtraction written above has a non-negative true value (32x-3x, 16x-x, 256x-x, 64x-8x, 32x-8x). No signal that leaves the module is moved inside a block: din and the six n_delay_regs keep their own nets, output_data_ready and the new_data_rdy enable are untouched, and only dout's expression changes. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line.

Registers and reset. No register is moved, added or removed. For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result are 0 before the rewrite and 0 after: the products and the whole reduction are combinational between the n_delay_reg/din registers and the dout register, inside the same new_data_rdy-enabled stage, in both versions. Because nothing is added, there is no register whose unknown initial value could be relied on, and the enabled dout/output_data_ready behaviour after any reset is unchanged.

Blocks, tiles, and block series. The rewrite instantiates 42 blocks, one per my_fir instance (7 modules x 6 h_fltr instances). At seed 1 the kept candidate packed 206 tiles with 144 blocks, i.e. 62 tiles for everything else (the fltr_compute 9x9 products); with 42 blocks the design should use 42 + 62 = 104 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 206 in the kept candidate. No block feeds another block: the longest series of blocks in any stage is 1, costing 2.14 ns plus about 1.3 ns of wire into it, inside a stage budgeted at about 9.3 ns.

Stage delay. The stage the rewrite leaves is the same my_fir register-to-register stage that is critical today. Its two longest shapes are: through the block, reg -> pair adder (1.00 + 0.40) -> wire 1.31 -> block 2.14 -> sum-tree adder (0.96 + 0.32) -> sum-tree adder (1.42 + 0.39) -> wire 1.18 + LUT 0.15 = about 9.3 ns, identical to the measured 9.354 ns path since nothing was added to it; and through the deepest soft tap, reg -> pair adder -> two constant-multiply adder levels -> two sum-tree adder levels -> LUT = 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 soft levels, about 9.2 ns at the 1.6 ns/level seen on the current critical path and about 7.7 ns at the 1.069 ns median. So no stage gets longer than the stage that is already slowest, and the slowest stage is expected to stay at or just below 9.35 ns; the next stages in the design are unchanged and were all at or below 9.35 ns in the kept candidate.

What soft logic leaves which stage, relative to the unmodified design. From the my_fir stage (the slowest stage, 11.607 ns in the baseline) the rewrite removes the six-deep chain of 28-bit adders that summed 6 or 7 products: it becomes three 17-bit pair adders, at most two constant-multiply adder levels per tap, and a two-level sum tree of 3 or 4 terms, i.e. depth 6 becomes depth 5 with one hop replaced by the block. One hard multiply per instance moves into the block; the other 5 or 6 hard multiplies of that instance are replaced by shift/add trees of 0 to 3 adders each. No other stage of the design is touched.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • my_fir_f1 1486$154, 1487$155, 1488$157, 1490$161, 1491$163, 1492$165; my_fir_f2 1542$169, 1543$170, 1545$174, 1547$178, 1548$180; my_fir_f3 1602$184, 1604$187, 1605$189, 1607$193; my_fir_h1 1661$197, 1662$198, 1665$204, 1666$206; my_fir_h2 1716$210, 1717$211, 1719$215, 1721$219, 1722$221; my_fir_h3 1775$225, 1776$226, 1779$232, 1780$234; my_fir_h4 1833$238, 1834$239, 1837$245, 1838$247 — left out of the blocks, but regrouped with their symmetric partners into the pair sums and computed outside the block as explicit shift/add trees, because the block offers only one multiply per DSP tile: giving each of these a block would cost 253779 apiece (about 9 CLBs) while its constant needs at most three 28-bit adders, roughly a fifth of that area, and a depth-2 tree is no slower than the block's 1.31 + 2.14 ns hop. Keeping them in blocks is exactly what makes the kept candidate's area 8.95e7 instead of about 6.9e7.
  • All 46 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 859$44 to 865$50, f2 889$58 to 895$64, f3 928$72 to 934$78, h1 959$86 to 965$92, h2 992$100 to 998$106, h3 1030$114 to 1036$120, h4 1065$128 to 1071$134) — left exactly as they are. They are 8-bit by 9-bit products that already pack four to a DSP tile on 39 tiles; one block each would need 7 tiles per instance (about 270 tiles overall, more than the device holds alongside the my_fir blocks) for products that are not on the critical path, since the products are registered in q1..q7 one stage before their sum and that sum stage was below both of the baseline's two slowest stages and below the 9.35 ns the rewritten my_fir leaves. Any block here would be paid for at about 9 CLBs and shorten nothing.

Expected effect on the objective. Against the kept candidate: 102 fewer DSP tiles (-2.59e7 area) against roughly 22 extra soft adders per h_fltr instance (+5e6), so about 6.9e7 used logic area (A/A0 about 0.70); period held at or just under 9.35 ns (D/D0 about 0.81); wirelength should fall further, since the removed blocks each routed a wide result out of a DSP tile and the replacements are local carry chains with hard-wired shifts. That puts the product near 0.50 of baseline against the kept candidate's 0.652. Even if the soft trees cost a full extra adder level and the period rose to 10.5 ns, the product would still be about 0.56, below the kept candidate.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

    wire[16:0] sum_06 = {1'b0, din} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg6};
    wire[16:0] sum_15 = {1'b0, n_delay_reg1} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg5};
    wire[16:0] sum_24 = {1'b0, n_delay_reg2} + {1'b0, n_delay_reg4};
    wire[27:0] x_06 = {11'b0, sum_06};
    wire[27:0] x_15 = {11'b0, sum_15};
    wire[27:0] x_24 = {11'b0, sum_24};
    wire[63:0] mult_res;

    comb_mult_add_16 tap_mult (.ax(n_delay_reg3), .ay(16'd235), .bx(32'b0), .result(mult_res));

    wire[27:0] term_06_a = (x_06 << 1) + x_06;
    wire[27:0] term_06 = (x_06 << 5) - term_06_a;
    wire[27:0] term_15_a = (x_15 << 1) + x_15;
    wire[27:0] term_15_b = (x_15 << 2) + x_15;
    wire[27:0] term_15 = (term_15_a << 5) + term_15_b;

You are the acceptance reviewer. You did not plan or write this edit. Check the edit against the approved plan, the block's contract and the correctness rules.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_mult_add_16 (precision INT16)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx
  • input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.

  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. PLAN:

Why this differs from the kept candidate (revision 1). Revision 1 put all three symmetric pair products plus the centre tap of every my_fir into blocks (144 blocks, 206 tiles). The seed-1 path it leaves is reg -> pair adder -> block -> adder -> adder -> LUT -> dffe = 9.354 ns, of which the block hop alone is 1.314 (wire) + 2.140 (block) = 3.45 ns. Every coefficient in these filters is a small constant (4, 9, 12, 15, 25, 29, 42, 56, 77, 101, 109, 148, 163, 193, 235, 255), and each has a shift/add form of depth at most 2, i.e. two soft adder levels, which on this design is about 2.1-3.2 ns — no slower than the single block hop it replaces, and far cheaper: a block takes a whole DSP tile (253779, about 9 CLBs), while two 28-bit carry-chain adders cost roughly a fifth of that. So blocks are kept only where they buy the most (one per instance, on the tap whose constant needs the deepest/widest shift-add tree), and the remaining taps of the same sum are computed outside the block. That trades 102 DSP tiles (-2.6e7 area) for about 22 extra soft adders per h_fltr instance (+5e6 area), with the stage delay unchanged.

Rewrite, per my_fir module (applied to the unmodified source; all six instances of each module inherit it). Insert before the existing always block, and replace only the dout <= ... expression inside it. All intermediates are 28-bit wires built by explicit zero-extension from the 17-bit pair sums, so every value is exact and the low 28 bits assigned to dout match the original dout exactly (the true sum is at most about 4.4e7 < 2^28, so no wrap occurs in either version; the shift/add forms are congruent mod 2^28 regardless).

  • Common to all seven: wire[16:0] s06, s15, s24 as above; wire[27:0] x0={11'b0,s06}, x1={11'b0,s15}, x2={11'b0,s24}; wire[63:0] r.
  • my_fir_f1 (29,101,15,235): block on the centre tap n_delay_reg3*235. Outside: t0a=(x0<<1)+x0; T0=(x0<<5)-t0a (=29*s06), t1a=(x1<<1)+x1; t1b=(x1<<2)+x1; T1=(t1a<<5)+t1b (=101*s15), T2=(x2<<4)-x2 (=15*s24), T3=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+(T2+T3);
  • my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (4,42,163,255): block on s24*163. Outside: T0=x0<<2 (=4*s06, no adder), t1a=(x1<<2)+x1; t1b=(x1<<4)+t1a; T1=t1b<<1 (=42*s15), T2=r[27:0], x3={12'b0,n_delay_reg3}; T3=(x3<<8)-x3 (=255*n_delay_reg3). dout <= (T0+T1)+(T2+T3);
  • my_fir_f3 (12,77,148): block on s15*77. Outside: T0=(x0<<3)+(x0<<2) (=12*s06), T1=r[27:0], t2a=(x2<<2)+x2; t2b=(x2<<5)+t2a; T2=t2b<<2 (=148*s24). dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;
  • my_fir_h1 (15,25,193): block on s24*193. Outside: T0=(x0<<4)-x0 (=15*s06), t1a=(x1<<5)-(x1<<3); T1=t1a+x1 (=25*s15), T2=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;
  • my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109): block on s24*109. Outside: T0=(x0<<3)+x0 (=9*s06), T1=(x1<<6)-(x1<<3) (=56*s15), T2=r[27:0]. dout <= (T0+T1)+T2;

Correctness. Each module's sum is symmetric (c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4), so din*c0+n6*c6 = s06*c0 and likewise for the other two pairs; the 6-tap modules (f3, h1, h3, h4) have c3=0 and omit n_delay_reg3 from the sum, which the rewrite keeps omitted (the register itself is still shifted, unchanged). For a pair fed to a block, s = 2*s[16:1] + s[0] and s[0] is the xor of the two addends' LSBs (there is no carry into bit 0), so ax*ay + bx = s[16:1]*2c + s[0]*c = s*c exactly; ax is 16 bits as required because the pair sum is 17 bits, and ay (154/218/326/386) and bx (at most 193) are well inside their ports. For my_fir_f1 the block takes the 16-bit register n_delay_reg3 directly with ay=235, so no split and no correction are needed and bx is tied to 0. The block is combinational, result is valid in the same cycle, and the result never approaches 2^64. Every subtraction written above has a non-negative true value (32x-3x, 16x-x, 256x-x, 64x-8x, 32x-8x). No signal that leaves the module is moved inside a block: din and the six n_delay_regs keep their own nets, output_data_ready and the new_data_rdy enable are untouched, and only dout's expression changes. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line.

Registers and reset. No register is moved, added or removed. For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result are 0 before the rewrite and 0 after: the products and the whole reduction are combinational between the n_delay_reg/din registers and the dout register, inside the same new_data_rdy-enabled stage, in both versions. Because nothing is added, there is no register whose unknown initial value could be relied on, and the enabled dout/output_data_ready behaviour after any reset is unchanged.

Blocks, tiles, and block series. The rewrite instantiates 42 blocks, one per my_fir instance (7 modules x 6 h_fltr instances). At seed 1 the kept candidate packed 206 tiles with 144 blocks, i.e. 62 tiles for everything else (the fltr_compute 9x9 products); with 42 blocks the design should use 42 + 62 = 104 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 206 in the kept candidate. No block feeds another block: the longest series of blocks in any stage is 1, costing 2.14 ns plus about 1.3 ns of wire into it, inside a stage budgeted at about 9.3 ns.

Stage delay. The stage the rewrite leaves is the same my_fir register-to-register stage that is critical today. Its two longest shapes are: through the block, reg -> pair adder (1.00 + 0.40) -> wire 1.31 -> block 2.14 -> sum-tree adder (0.96 + 0.32) -> sum-tree adder (1.42 + 0.39) -> wire 1.18 + LUT 0.15 = about 9.3 ns, identical to the measured 9.354 ns path since nothing was added to it; and through the deepest soft tap, reg -> pair adder -> two constant-multiply adder levels -> two sum-tree adder levels -> LUT = 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 soft levels, about 9.2 ns at the 1.6 ns/level seen on the current critical path and about 7.7 ns at the 1.069 ns median. So no stage gets longer than the stage that is already slowest, and the slowest stage is expected to stay at or just below 9.35 ns; the next stages in the design are unchanged and were all at or below 9.35 ns in the kept candidate.

What soft logic leaves which stage, relative to the unmodified design. From the my_fir stage (the slowest stage, 11.607 ns in the baseline) the rewrite removes the six-deep chain of 28-bit adders that summed 6 or 7 products: it becomes three 17-bit pair adders, at most two constant-multiply adder levels per tap, and a two-level sum tree of 3 or 4 terms, i.e. depth 6 becomes depth 5 with one hop replaced by the block. One hard multiply per instance moves into the block; the other 5 or 6 hard multiplies of that instance are replaced by shift/add trees of 0 to 3 adders each. No other stage of the design is touched.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • my_fir_f1 1486$154, 1487$155, 1488$157, 1490$161, 1491$163, 1492$165; my_fir_f2 1542$169, 1543$170, 1545$174, 1547$178, 1548$180; my_fir_f3 1602$184, 1604$187, 1605$189, 1607$193; my_fir_h1 1661$197, 1662$198, 1665$204, 1666$206; my_fir_h2 1716$210, 1717$211, 1719$215, 1721$219, 1722$221; my_fir_h3 1775$225, 1776$226, 1779$232, 1780$234; my_fir_h4 1833$238, 1834$239, 1837$245, 1838$247 — left out of the blocks, but regrouped with their symmetric partners into the pair sums and computed outside the block as explicit shift/add trees, because the block offers only one multiply per DSP tile: giving each of these a block would cost 253779 apiece (about 9 CLBs) while its constant needs at most three 28-bit adders, roughly a fifth of that area, and a depth-2 tree is no slower than the block's 1.31 + 2.14 ns hop. Keeping them in blocks is exactly what makes the kept candidate's area 8.95e7 instead of about 6.9e7.
  • All 46 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 859$44 to 865$50, f2 889$58 to 895$64, f3 928$72 to 934$78, h1 959$86 to 965$92, h2 992$100 to 998$106, h3 1030$114 to 1036$120, h4 1065$128 to 1071$134) — left exactly as they are. They are 8-bit by 9-bit products that already pack four to a DSP tile on 39 tiles; one block each would need 7 tiles per instance (about 270 tiles overall, more than the device holds alongside the my_fir blocks) for products that are not on the critical path, since the products are registered in q1..q7 one stage before their sum and that sum stage was below both of the baseline's two slowest stages and below the 9.35 ns the rewritten my_fir leaves. Any block here would be paid for at about 9 CLBs and shorten nothing.

Expected effect on the objective. Against the kept candidate: 102 fewer DSP tiles (-2.59e7 area) against roughly 22 extra soft adders per h_fltr instance (+5e6), so about 6.9e7 used logic area (A/A0 about 0.70); period held at or just under 9.35 ns (D/D0 about 0.81); wirelength should fall further, since the removed blocks each routed a wide result out of a DSP tile and the replacements are local carry chains with hard-wired shifts. That puts the product near 0.50 of baseline against the kept candidate's 0.652. Even if the soft trees cost a full extra adder level and the period rose to 10.5 ns, the product would still be about 0.56, below the kept candidate.

DESIGN_CHANGE: each my_fir's din is a fltr_compute output d_out_tmp[18:3], whose value is bounded by the 8-bit pixel input times the filter's coefficient sum (at most 21451 for the modules feeding my_fir_f1/f2/h1/h2/h3/h4), so for all but my_fir_f3 the 17-bit pair sum would fit in 16 bits. If the design declared that bound (or narrowed those douts), the block could take the pair sum directly on ax with ay the plain coefficient, dropping the [16:1] split and the bx correction term entirely.

No other module changed; one block instance per module → 42 instances via the 6 h_fltr copies, as planned.
  • Ports. Every instance connects ax, ay, bx, result by name with correct widths: ax is 16 bits (n_delay_reg3 or sum_xx[16:1]), bx is {23'b0, 9-bit} or 32'b0, result is a 64-bit wire whose [27:0] is one term of the dout sum, exactly as the plan states.
  • Terms. Coefficients match the testbench defines (b: 29,101,15,235; c/2: 4,42,163,255; d: 12,77,148,0; 1: 15,25,193,0; 3/4: 9,56,109,0). Shift/add forms are each exact: 32x−3x=29x, 3x·32+5x=101x, 16x−x=15x, 4x, (16x+5x)·2=42x, 256x−x=255x, 8x+4x=12x, (32x+5x)·4=148x, 16x−x=15x, (32x−8x)+x=25x, 8x+x=9x, 64x−8x=56x. Each block gives 2c·s[16:1] + c·s[0] = c·s since s[0] = n_a[0]^n_b[0] with no carry into bit 0, and ay is 2c (326/386/218/154) with bx the c correction (163/193/109/77). The symmetric regrouping is valid because c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4; the c3=0 modules correctly omit n_delay_reg3.
  • Widths. dout is 28 bits (1462 etc.). Every intermediate is a 28-bit wire; all shifted values and all partial sums stay below 2^28 (worst case ≈4.4e7), and every subtraction has a non-negative true value, so no truncation or borrow differs from the original, which also fits in 28 bits.
  • Visibility. Nothing that leaves the module moved inside a block: din and all n_delay_reg* keep their own nets and still feed the shift chain and each other; output_data_ready and the new_data_rdy enable are untouched; only the mult_res term is read out of the block.

1	// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
6	// reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_mult_add_16 (
8	    input  [15:0] ax,
9	    input  [15:0] ay,
10	    input  [31:0] bx,
11	    output [63:0] result
12	);
13	
14	    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
15	    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact
16	
17	    assign result = sum;
18	
19	endmodule

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_mult_add_16 (precision INT16)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx
  • input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • The block's internal delay is fixed. Soft logic between a block's output and the next register adds to that stage; blocks in series each add their delay plus a wire.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.

This is a revision of the kept candidate (revision 2). It keeps exactly the same block census (42 blocks, one per my_fir instance, 101 DSP tiles) and the same block operands for six of the seven modules; what changes is where the block's result enters the sum and the shape of the soft tree, which is what the measured seed-1 path shows to be costing the period.

Why the kept candidate is 8.16 ns, element by element (from the reported path): reg -> xor LUT (1.229) -> wire into bx (1.209) -> block (2.140) -> adder level (0.888) -> adder level (1.474) -> output LUT + wire (1.126) -> setup. That is pre-block logic of 2.44 ns and two 28-bit adder levels after the block. The rewrite below leaves exactly one adder level between the block and the dout register, and balances the purely-soft side so it arrives no later than the block does. Predicted slowest rewritten stage: soft side ready after 4 levels (0.10 + 4x1.2 = 4.9 ns), block result ready at 4.65-4.68 ns (pair-sum/xor level 1.3 + wire 1.21 + block 2.14), final 28-bit adder 1.2 ns, output LUT + wire + setup 1.13 ns => about 7.2-7.3 ns, against the 8.16 ns the kept candidate leaves. The same model reproduces the kept candidate's measured path to within 0.05 ns (2.54+2.14+1.2+1.2+1.13 = 8.21 vs 8.16 measured), so the 7.2-7.3 ns estimate is on the same footing.

Per-module arithmetic the editor must write (all wires 28 bit; every value below is unsigned and every add/sub is mod 2^28, which is exactly what the original 28-bit dout assignment does, since din and the delay registers are unsigned 16-bit and every coefficient is a positive constant). Write each level as its own named wire so the tree shape survives synthesis; put the assignments outside the always block and leave the always block otherwise untouched (same enable new_data_rdy, same delay-register chain, same output_data_ready).

my_fir_f1 (coefficients 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; A=din+n_delay_reg6, B=n_delay_reg1+n_delay_reg5, C=n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4, D=n_delay_reg3):
block = 235*D + 32*A;
p_b96 = (x_15<<6)+(x_15<<5); p_b5 = (x_15<<2)+x_15; p_c15 = (x_24<<4)-x_24; p_a3 = (x_06<<1)+x_06;
q_b101 = p_b96+p_b5; q_ca = p_c15-p_a3; soft_sum = q_b101+q_ca;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 235D + 32A + 101B + 15C - 3A = 29A+101B+15C+235D, the original sum.

my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (4,42,163,255,163,42,4): block = 326*floor(C/2) + 163*(C mod 2) = 163*C (326*sum_24[16:1] + 163*(n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) is exactly 163*(n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4));
p_b40 = (x_15<<5)+(x_15<<3); p_d255 = (x_3<<8)-x_3; p_a4b2 = (x_06<<2)+(x_15<<1);
q_ab = p_b40+p_a4b2; soft_sum = q_ab+p_d255;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 4A+42B+163C+255D.

my_fir_f3 (12,77,148,0,148,77,12): block = 148*C;
p_a12 = (x_06<<3)+(x_06<<2); p_b72 = (x_15<<6)+(x_15<<3); p_b5 = (x_15<<2)+x_15;
q_b77 = p_b72+p_b5; soft_sum = q_b77+p_a12;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 12A+77B+148C (the original omits the n_delay_reg3 tap, line 1602-1607).

my_fir_h1 (15,25,193,0,193,25,15): block = 193*C;
p_a15 = (x_06<<4)-x_06; p_b24 = (x_15<<4)+(x_15<<3);
q_ab = p_a15+p_b24; soft_sum = q_ab+x_15;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 15A+25B+193C.

my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109,0,109,56,9): block = 109*C;
p_a9 = (x_06<<3)+x_06; p_b56 = (x_15<<6)-(x_15<<3); soft_sum = p_a9+p_b56;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 9A+56B+109C.

Correctness. Every my_fir coefficient set is symmetric (c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4), so pairing is exact; sum_24[16:1] is floor((n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4)/2) < 2^16 and fits ax, and the xor term restores the dropped low bit, so the block's unsigned product is the exact pair term. ay constants 235, 326, 296, 386, 218 are all < 2^16; the largest bx is 32*(din+n_delay_reg6) < 2^22, so nothing wraps inside the block's 64-bit result and only result[27:0] is used. All regrouping is addition/subtraction mod 2^28, which matches the original truncation into the 28-bit dout. No design register is moved, removed or added, no reset behaviour changes, and nothing inside a block is read anywhere else: mult_res is local to its instance and only dout leaves the module. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line.

Blocks added and tiles. 42 blocks, one per my_fir instance (7 modules x 6 instances through h_fltr, lines 514-520), each on its own DSP tile; the 294 fltr_compute 9x9 products stay packed four to a tile. Design total 101 DSP tiles (measured census of the kept candidate, which this revision matches exactly), against 224 in the baseline. Block count, tile count and soft-adder count per instance are the same as or one adder below the kept candidate (f1 goes from 9 to 8 28-bit adders, the others are unchanged), so area and wirelength should land on the kept candidate's figures and the gain is the period.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. A block never feeds another block; each block's result goes through a single 28-bit adder into the dout register. Block contribution to the stage is 2.14 ns of the ~7.3 ns stage; the rest is 1.3 ns of pair-sum/xor level ahead of it, 1.21 ns of wire into it, 1.2 ns for the one adder after it, and 1.13 ns of output LUT, wire and setup.

What soft logic leaves which stage. The stage affected is the my_fir dout stage, which is the baseline's slowest stage (11.6069 ns, my_fir_f1) and the second slowest (11.293 ns, my_fir_f2), and is still the slowest stage the kept candidate leaves (8.16 ns at seed 1). Out of it go: one hard 18x19 multiply per converted tap and, compared with the kept candidate, one full 28-bit adder level on the block's own path (the block result is now the last term of the sum rather than an input two levels deep). What stays in soft logic is the shift/add tree for the taps the block does not carry, now balanced so that it is ready at the same moment the block result is. Nothing is added to any other stage: the delay-register chain, output_data_ready, and the h_fltr/steer_fltr stages are untouched.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region. Before: the products are unregistered (the table's "products registered 0 stage(s) before the sum"); operands are din and the delay registers, the seven products and their six-level adder chain are combinational, and the result is captured in dout — one register stage from operands to result. After: identical — one register stage from operands to result. The block is combinational, no design register becomes a block register, no register is moved, and no register is added, so latency and reset behaviour are bit-for-bit unchanged on every cycle.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • All 42 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071) are left, for three reasons that apply to all of them equally. (i) They already sit four to a DSP tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt mode on 39 tiles; a block takes a tile alone, so converting even one 8-bit-by-9-bit product would pay a whole tile (253779, about 9 clusters) to save a quarter of one, and converting all of them would cost roughly 250 extra tiles. (ii) Their products are registered one stage before the sum (q1..q7 at line 867 etc.), so a block placed on a product cannot absorb any level of the q -> d_out_tmp adder chain, which is the only part of fltr_compute near the critical path; the stage a block would shorten (din slice -> q) is already short. (iii) Each term enters the 20-bit sum as the sign-extension of a 17-bit truncated product ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at line 867), i.e. the term is not the plain unsigned product the block computes; reproducing it needs a per-term 2^17 correction derived from the product's bit 16, which would add logic to the very stage that is already the long one there.
  • Within the converted my_fir modules, the taps not named in REGIONS (my_fir_f1 1486,1487,1488,1490,1491,1492; my_fir_f2 1542,1543,1545,1547,1548; my_fir_f3 1602,1603,1606,1607; my_fir_h1 1661,1662,1665,1666; my_fir_h2 1716,1717,1719,1721,1722; my_fir_h3 1775,1776,1779,1780; my_fir_h4 1833,1834,1837,1838) are not carried by a block: each block has one product port, and these taps are recomputed outside it as the shift/add trees above, which is what makes the regrouping legal. A second block per instance was considered and rejected: it adds 42 tiles and does not shorten the stage, because the pair-sum block's result cannot arrive before about 4.68 ns and the final adder and output LUT after it are unavoidable, so the stage stays at about 7.0-7.2 ns either way.

Risk the plan accepts. The untouched fltr_compute q -> d_out_tmp stage is a chain of six 20-bit adder levels (line 867 and its six siblings); by the same per-level figure it is worth roughly 7.0-7.9 ns, so it may floor the period somewhere in that band and the measured gain may be smaller than the 8.16 -> 7.3 ns the rewritten stage gives. Nothing in this revision makes that stage worse, and area and wirelength are held at the kept candidate's values, so the expected product moves down, not up.

DESIGN_CHANGE: the seven fltr_compute modules sum their seven sign-extended terms as a left-associated chain (line 867 and its siblings at 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), which synthesises to six adder levels between the q registers and d_out_tmp. Writing that same sum as a balanced tree — the value is identical, since all seven terms are 20-bit values added mod 2^20 — would cut that stage from six levels to three, roughly 3.5 ns, and would remove the floor that now limits what any my_fir rewrite can deliver. It needs no block and is not part of this rewrite, so it is not done here.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

The plan

I'll read the design source first.

TIER: T2
REGIONS: my_fir_f1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1489$159, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1544$172, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1546$176, my_fir_f3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1604$187, my_fir_f3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1605$189, my_fir_h1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1663$200, my_fir_h1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1664$202, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1718$213, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1720$217, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1777$228, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1778$230, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1835$241, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1836$243
SHARED_REDUCTION: the dout sum of each my_fir module — seven reductions, one per module (my_fir_f1 1486-1492, my_fir_f2 1542-1548, my_fir_f3 1602-1607, my_fir_h1 1661-1666, my_fir_h2 1716-1722, my_fir_h3 1775-1780, my_fir_h4 1833-1838), each instantiated 6 times through h_fltr (lines 514-520)
BLOCKS: 42
TILES: 101
STAGE_NS: 7.3
MAPPING: one block per my_fir instance. Pair sums (17 bit, unsigned) sum_06={1'b0,din}+{1'b0,n_delay_reg6}, sum_15={1'b0,n_delay_reg1}+{1'b0,n_delay_reg5}, sum_24={1'b0,n_delay_reg2}+{1'b0,n_delay_reg4}; x_06={11'b0,sum_06}, x_15={11'b0,sum_15}, x_24={11'b0,sum_24}, x_3={12'b0,n_delay_reg3} (28 bit). my_fir_f1: .ax(n_delay_reg3) .ay(16'd235) .bx({10'b0, sum_06, 5'b0}) — the block carries the centre tap 235*n_delay_reg3 plus 32*(din+n_delay_reg6). my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2: .ax(sum_24[16:1]) .ay(16'd326) .bx({23'b0,(n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) ? 9'd163 : 9'd0}). my_fir_f3: .ax(sum_24[16:1]) .ay(16'd296) .bx({23'b0,(n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) ? 9'd148 : 9'd0}). my_fir_h1: .ax(sum_24[16:1]) .ay(16'd386) .bx({23'b0,(n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) ? 9'd193 : 9'd0}). my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4: .ax(sum_24[16:1]) .ay(16'd218) .bx({23'b0,(n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) ? 9'd109 : 9'd0}). In every instance .result(mult_res) is a 64-bit wire and only mult_res[27:0] is used, as the last term added into dout.
PLAN:

This is a revision of the kept candidate (revision 2). It keeps exactly the same block census (42 blocks, one per my_fir instance, 101 DSP tiles) and the same block operands for six of the seven modules; what changes is where the block's result enters the sum and the shape of the soft tree, which is what the measured seed-1 path shows to be costing the period.

Why the kept candidate is 8.16 ns, element by element (from the reported path): reg -> xor LUT (1.229) -> wire into bx (1.209) -> block (2.140) -> adder level (0.888) -> adder level (1.474) -> output LUT + wire (1.126) -> setup. That is pre-block logic of 2.44 ns and two 28-bit adder levels after the block. The rewrite below leaves exactly one adder level between the block and the dout register, and balances the purely-soft side so it arrives no later than the block does. Predicted slowest rewritten stage: soft side ready after 4 levels (0.10 + 4x1.2 = 4.9 ns), block result ready at 4.65-4.68 ns (pair-sum/xor level 1.3 + wire 1.21 + block 2.14), final 28-bit adder 1.2 ns, output LUT + wire + setup 1.13 ns => about 7.2-7.3 ns, against the 8.16 ns the kept candidate leaves. The same model reproduces the kept candidate's measured path to within 0.05 ns (2.54+2.14+1.2+1.2+1.13 = 8.21 vs 8.16 measured), so the 7.2-7.3 ns estimate is on the same footing.

Per-module arithmetic the editor must write (all wires 28 bit; every value below is unsigned and every add/sub is mod 2^28, which is exactly what the original 28-bit dout assignment does, since din and the delay registers are unsigned 16-bit and every coefficient is a positive constant). Write each level as its own named wire so the tree shape survives synthesis; put the assignments outside the always block and leave the always block otherwise untouched (same enable new_data_rdy, same delay-register chain, same output_data_ready).

my_fir_f1 (coefficients 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; A=din+n_delay_reg6, B=n_delay_reg1+n_delay_reg5, C=n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4, D=n_delay_reg3):
block = 235*D + 32*A;
p_b96 = (x_15<<6)+(x_15<<5); p_b5 = (x_15<<2)+x_15; p_c15 = (x_24<<4)-x_24; p_a3 = (x_06<<1)+x_06;
q_b101 = p_b96+p_b5; q_ca = p_c15-p_a3; soft_sum = q_b101+q_ca;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 235D + 32A + 101B + 15C - 3A = 29A+101B+15C+235D, the original sum.

my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (4,42,163,255,163,42,4): block = 326*floor(C/2) + 163*(C mod 2) = 163*C (326*sum_24[16:1] + 163*(n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) is exactly 163*(n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4));
p_b40 = (x_15<<5)+(x_15<<3); p_d255 = (x_3<<8)-x_3; p_a4b2 = (x_06<<2)+(x_15<<1);
q_ab = p_b40+p_a4b2; soft_sum = q_ab+p_d255;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 4A+42B+163C+255D.

my_fir_f3 (12,77,148,0,148,77,12): block = 148*C;
p_a12 = (x_06<<3)+(x_06<<2); p_b72 = (x_15<<6)+(x_15<<3); p_b5 = (x_15<<2)+x_15;
q_b77 = p_b72+p_b5; soft_sum = q_b77+p_a12;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 12A+77B+148C (the original omits the n_delay_reg3 tap, line 1602-1607).

my_fir_h1 (15,25,193,0,193,25,15): block = 193*C;
p_a15 = (x_06<<4)-x_06; p_b24 = (x_15<<4)+(x_15<<3);
q_ab = p_a15+p_b24; soft_sum = q_ab+x_15;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 15A+25B+193C.

my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109,0,109,56,9): block = 109*C;
p_a9 = (x_06<<3)+x_06; p_b56 = (x_15<<6)-(x_15<<3); soft_sum = p_a9+p_b56;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 9A+56B+109C.

Correctness. Every my_fir coefficient set is symmetric (c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4), so pairing is exact; sum_24[16:1] is floor((n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4)/2) < 2^16 and fits ax, and the xor term restores the dropped low bit, so the block's unsigned product is the exact pair term. ay constants 235, 326, 296, 386, 218 are all < 2^16; the largest bx is 32*(din+n_delay_reg6) < 2^22, so nothing wraps inside the block's 64-bit result and only result[27:0] is used. All regrouping is addition/subtraction mod 2^28, which matches the original truncation into the 28-bit dout. No design register is moved, removed or added, no reset behaviour changes, and nothing inside a block is read anywhere else: mult_res is local to its instance and only dout leaves the module. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line.

Blocks added and tiles. 42 blocks, one per my_fir instance (7 modules x 6 instances through h_fltr, lines 514-520), each on its own DSP tile; the 294 fltr_compute 9x9 products stay packed four to a tile. Design total 101 DSP tiles (measured census of the kept candidate, which this revision matches exactly), against 224 in the baseline. Block count, tile count and soft-adder count per instance are the same as or one adder below the kept candidate (f1 goes from 9 to 8 28-bit adders, the others are unchanged), so area and wirelength should land on the kept candidate's figures and the gain is the period.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. A block never feeds another block; each block's result goes through a single 28-bit adder into the dout register. Block contribution to the stage is 2.14 ns of the ~7.3 ns stage; the rest is 1.3 ns of pair-sum/xor level ahead of it, 1.21 ns of wire into it, 1.2 ns for the one adder after it, and 1.13 ns of output LUT, wire and setup.

What soft logic leaves which stage. The stage affected is the my_fir dout stage, which is the baseline's slowest stage (11.6069 ns, my_fir_f1) and the second slowest (11.293 ns, my_fir_f2), and is still the slowest stage the kept candidate leaves (8.16 ns at seed 1). Out of it go: one hard 18x19 multiply per converted tap and, compared with the kept candidate, one full 28-bit adder level on the block's own path (the block result is now the last term of the sum rather than an input two levels deep). What stays in soft logic is the shift/add tree for the taps the block does not carry, now balanced so that it is ready at the same moment the block result is. Nothing is added to any other stage: the delay-register chain, output_data_ready, and the h_fltr/steer_fltr stages are untouched.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region. Before: the products are unregistered (the table's "products registered 0 stage(s) before the sum"); operands are din and the delay registers, the seven products and their six-level adder chain are combinational, and the result is captured in dout — one register stage from operands to result. After: identical — one register stage from operands to result. The block is combinational, no design register becomes a block register, no register is moved, and no register is added, so latency and reset behaviour are bit-for-bit unchanged on every cycle.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • All 42 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071) are left, for three reasons that apply to all of them equally. (i) They already sit four to a DSP tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt mode on 39 tiles; a block takes a tile alone, so converting even one 8-bit-by-9-bit product would pay a whole tile (253779, about 9 clusters) to save a quarter of one, and converting all of them would cost roughly 250 extra tiles. (ii) Their products are registered one stage before the sum (q1..q7 at line 867 etc.), so a block placed on a product cannot absorb any level of the q -> d_out_tmp adder chain, which is the only part of fltr_compute near the critical path; the stage a block would shorten (din slice -> q) is already short. (iii) Each term enters the 20-bit sum as the sign-extension of a 17-bit truncated product ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at line 867), i.e. the term is not the plain unsigned product the block computes; reproducing it needs a per-term 2^17 correction derived from the product's bit 16, which would add logic to the very stage that is already the long one there.
  • Within the converted my_fir modules, the taps not named in REGIONS (my_fir_f1 1486,1487,1488,1490,1491,1492; my_fir_f2 1542,1543,1545,1547,1548; my_fir_f3 1602,1603,1606,1607; my_fir_h1 1661,1662,1665,1666; my_fir_h2 1716,1717,1719,1721,1722; my_fir_h3 1775,1776,1779,1780; my_fir_h4 1833,1834,1837,1838) are not carried by a block: each block has one product port, and these taps are recomputed outside it as the shift/add trees above, which is what makes the regrouping legal. A second block per instance was considered and rejected: it adds 42 tiles and does not shorten the stage, because the pair-sum block's result cannot arrive before about 4.68 ns and the final adder and output LUT after it are unavoidable, so the stage stays at about 7.0-7.2 ns either way.

Risk the plan accepts. The untouched fltr_compute q -> d_out_tmp stage is a chain of six 20-bit adder levels (line 867 and its six siblings); by the same per-level figure it is worth roughly 7.0-7.9 ns, so it may floor the period somewhere in that band and the measured gain may be smaller than the 8.16 -> 7.3 ns the rewritten stage gives. Nothing in this revision makes that stage worse, and area and wirelength are held at the kept candidate's values, so the expected product moves down, not up.

DESIGN_CHANGE: the seven fltr_compute modules sum their seven sign-extended terms as a left-associated chain (line 867 and its siblings at 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), which synthesises to six adder levels between the q registers and d_out_tmp. Writing that same sum as a balanced tree — the value is identical, since all seven terms are 20-bit values added mod 2^20 — would cut that stage from six levels to three, roughly 3.5 ns, and would remove the floor that now limits what any my_fir rewrite can deliver. It needs no block and is not part of this rewrite, so it is not done here.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_mult_add_16.v) are in sim_reference/.

Checked against the source: all seven my_fir coefficient sets are symmetric (29,101,15,235,…; 4,42,163,255,…; 12,77,148,0,…; 15,25,193,0,…; 9,56,109,0,… at lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), WIDTH_5B=16 (line 1451), so each sum_xx[16:1] fits ax and the xor restores the dropped bit; each stated ay is twice its coefficient and each bx constant is the coefficient, so every block term equals the exact pair product. Each per-module shift/add tree reconstructs the remaining taps exactly, and all regrouping is mod 2^28, matching the 28-bit dout truncation (f3/h1/h3/h4 correctly omit the absent n_delay_reg3 tap, lines 1602-1607, 1661-1666, 1775-1780, 1833-1838). No register is moved or added, the always bodies and new_data_rdy enable are untouched, mult_res is local and only dout/output_data_ready leave each module, and no ASSUMES is needed. 42 blocks = 7 modules × 6 h_fltr instances (188-190, 195-197, 514-520). The left candidates are fully covered by line range with reasons (the fltr_compute claims about registered q1..q7 and the {q[16],q[16],q[16],q} 20-bit sum check out at 859-867 and siblings), and the block-count/tile, block-depth, soft-logic-stage and register-stage items are all stated.

Task

Edit stereovision2.v in this directory to carry out the approved plan below: rewrite the regions it names onto the hard block described next. If a step cannot be done as the plan says, stop and say which step and why; do not improvise a different rewrite.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: comb_mult_add_16 (precision INT16)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx
  • input ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32]
  • output ports: result[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: none; the block is combinational, and result is valid in the same cycle the inputs are applied.
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above.
The design
  • Regions in the approved plan: my_fir_f1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1489$159, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1544$172, my_fir_f2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1546$176, my_fir_f3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1604$187, my_fir_f3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1605$189, my_fir_h1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1663$200, my_fir_h1.$mul$stereovision2.v:1664$202, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1718$213, my_fir_h2.$mul$stereovision2.v:1720$217, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1777$228, my_fir_h3.$mul$stereovision2.v:1778$230, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1835$241, my_fir_h4.$mul$stereovision2.v:1836$243. Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it.
