PLAN:

This is a revision of the kept candidate (revision 2). It keeps exactly the same block census (42 blocks, one per my_fir instance, 101 DSP tiles) and the same block operands for six of the seven modules; what changes is where the block's result enters the sum and the shape of the soft tree, which is what the measured seed-1 path shows to be costing the period.

Why the kept candidate is 8.16 ns, element by element (from the reported path): reg -> xor LUT (1.229) -> wire into bx (1.209) -> block (2.140) -> adder level (0.888) -> adder level (1.474) -> output LUT + wire (1.126) -> setup. That is pre-block logic of 2.44 ns and two 28-bit adder levels after the block. The rewrite below leaves exactly one adder level between the block and the dout register, and balances the purely-soft side so it arrives no later than the block does. Predicted slowest rewritten stage: soft side ready after 4 levels (0.10 + 4x1.2 = 4.9 ns), block result ready at 4.65-4.68 ns (pair-sum/xor level 1.3 + wire 1.21 + block 2.14), final 28-bit adder 1.2 ns, output LUT + wire + setup 1.13 ns => about 7.2-7.3 ns, against the 8.16 ns the kept candidate leaves. The same model reproduces the kept candidate's measured path to within 0.05 ns (2.54+2.14+1.2+1.2+1.13 = 8.21 vs 8.16 measured), so the 7.2-7.3 ns estimate is on the same footing.

Per-module arithmetic the editor must write (all wires 28 bit; every value below is unsigned and every add/sub is mod 2^28, which is exactly what the original 28-bit dout assignment does, since din and the delay registers are unsigned 16-bit and every coefficient is a positive constant). Write each level as its own named wire so the tree shape survives synthesis; put the assignments outside the always block and leave the always block otherwise untouched (same enable new_data_rdy, same delay-register chain, same output_data_ready).

my_fir_f1 (coefficients 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; A=din+n_delay_reg6, B=n_delay_reg1+n_delay_reg5, C=n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4, D=n_delay_reg3):
block = 235*D + 32*A;
p_b96 = (x_15<<6)+(x_15<<5); p_b5 = (x_15<<2)+x_15; p_c15 = (x_24<<4)-x_24; p_a3 = (x_06<<1)+x_06;
q_b101 = p_b96+p_b5; q_ca = p_c15-p_a3; soft_sum = q_b101+q_ca;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 235D + 32A + 101B + 15C - 3A = 29A+101B+15C+235D, the original sum.

my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (4,42,163,255,163,42,4): block = 326*floor(C/2) + 163*(C mod 2) = 163*C (326*sum_24[16:1] + 163*(n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) is exactly 163*(n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4));
p_b40 = (x_15<<5)+(x_15<<3); p_d255 = (x_3<<8)-x_3; p_a4b2 = (x_06<<2)+(x_15<<1);
q_ab = p_b40+p_a4b2; soft_sum = q_ab+p_d255;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 4A+42B+163C+255D.

my_fir_f3 (12,77,148,0,148,77,12): block = 148*C;
p_a12 = (x_06<<3)+(x_06<<2); p_b72 = (x_15<<6)+(x_15<<3); p_b5 = (x_15<<2)+x_15;
q_b77 = p_b72+p_b5; soft_sum = q_b77+p_a12;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 12A+77B+148C (the original omits the n_delay_reg3 tap, line 1602-1607).

my_fir_h1 (15,25,193,0,193,25,15): block = 193*C;
p_a15 = (x_06<<4)-x_06; p_b24 = (x_15<<4)+(x_15<<3);
q_ab = p_a15+p_b24; soft_sum = q_ab+x_15;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 15A+25B+193C.

my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109,0,109,56,9): block = 109*C;
p_a9 = (x_06<<3)+x_06; p_b56 = (x_15<<6)-(x_15<<3); soft_sum = p_a9+p_b56;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 9A+56B+109C.

Correctness. Every my_fir coefficient set is symmetric (c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4), so pairing is exact; sum_24[16:1] is floor((n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4)/2) < 2^16 and fits ax, and the xor term restores the dropped low bit, so the block's unsigned product is the exact pair term. ay constants 235, 326, 296, 386, 218 are all < 2^16; the largest bx is 32*(din+n_delay_reg6) < 2^22, so nothing wraps inside the block's 64-bit result and only result[27:0] is used. All regrouping is addition/subtraction mod 2^28, which matches the original truncation into the 28-bit dout. No design register is moved, removed or added, no reset behaviour changes, and nothing inside a block is read anywhere else: mult_res is local to its instance and only dout leaves the module. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line.

Blocks added and tiles. 42 blocks, one per my_fir instance (7 modules x 6 instances through h_fltr, lines 514-520), each on its own DSP tile; the 294 fltr_compute 9x9 products stay packed four to a tile. Design total 101 DSP tiles (measured census of the kept candidate, which this revision matches exactly), against 224 in the baseline. Block count, tile count and soft-adder count per instance are the same as or one adder below the kept candidate (f1 goes from 9 to 8 28-bit adders, the others are unchanged), so area and wirelength should land on the kept candidate's figures and the gain is the period.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. A block never feeds another block; each block's result goes through a single 28-bit adder into the dout register. Block contribution to the stage is 2.14 ns of the ~7.3 ns stage; the rest is 1.3 ns of pair-sum/xor level ahead of it, 1.21 ns of wire into it, 1.2 ns for the one adder after it, and 1.13 ns of output LUT, wire and setup.

What soft logic leaves which stage. The stage affected is the my_fir dout stage, which is the baseline's slowest stage (11.6069 ns, my_fir_f1) and the second slowest (11.293 ns, my_fir_f2), and is still the slowest stage the kept candidate leaves (8.16 ns at seed 1). Out of it go: one hard 18x19 multiply per converted tap and, compared with the kept candidate, one full 28-bit adder level on the block's own path (the block result is now the last term of the sum rather than an input two levels deep). What stays in soft logic is the shift/add tree for the taps the block does not carry, now balanced so that it is ready at the same moment the block result is. Nothing is added to any other stage: the delay-register chain, output_data_ready, and the h_fltr/steer_fltr stages are untouched.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region. Before: the products are unregistered (the table's "products registered 0 stage(s) before the sum"); operands are din and the delay registers, the seven products and their six-level adder chain are combinational, and the result is captured in dout — one register stage from operands to result. After: identical — one register stage from operands to result. The block is combinational, no design register becomes a block register, no register is moved, and no register is added, so latency and reset behaviour are bit-for-bit unchanged on every cycle.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • All 42 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071) are left, for three reasons that apply to all of them equally. (i) They already sit four to a DSP tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt mode on 39 tiles; a block takes a tile alone, so converting even one 8-bit-by-9-bit product would pay a whole tile (253779, about 9 clusters) to save a quarter of one, and converting all of them would cost roughly 250 extra tiles. (ii) Their products are registered one stage before the sum (q1..q7 at line 867 etc.), so a block placed on a product cannot absorb any level of the q -> d_out_tmp adder chain, which is the only part of fltr_compute near the critical path; the stage a block would shorten (din slice -> q) is already short. (iii) Each term enters the 20-bit sum as the sign-extension of a 17-bit truncated product ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at line 867), i.e. the term is not the plain unsigned product the block computes; reproducing it needs a per-term 2^17 correction derived from the product's bit 16, which would add logic to the very stage that is already the long one there.
  • Within the converted my_fir modules, the taps not named in REGIONS (my_fir_f1 1486,1487,1488,1490,1491,1492; my_fir_f2 1542,1543,1545,1547,1548; my_fir_f3 1602,1603,1606,1607; my_fir_h1 1661,1662,1665,1666; my_fir_h2 1716,1717,1719,1721,1722; my_fir_h3 1775,1776,1779,1780; my_fir_h4 1833,1834,1837,1838) are not carried by a block: each block has one product port, and these taps are recomputed outside it as the shift/add trees above, which is what makes the regrouping legal. A second block per instance was considered and rejected: it adds 42 tiles and does not shorten the stage, because the pair-sum block's result cannot arrive before about 4.68 ns and the final adder and output LUT after it are unavoidable, so the stage stays at about 7.0-7.2 ns either way.

Risk the plan accepts. The untouched fltr_compute q -> d_out_tmp stage is a chain of six 20-bit adder levels (line 867 and its six siblings); by the same per-level figure it is worth roughly 7.0-7.9 ns, so it may floor the period somewhere in that band and the measured gain may be smaller than the 8.16 -> 7.3 ns the rewritten stage gives. Nothing in this revision makes that stage worse, and area and wirelength are held at the kept candidate's values, so the expected product moves down, not up.

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (comb_mult_add_16.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

  • my_fir_h3 (1777$228, 1778$230) and my_fir_h4 (1835$241, 1836$243) — block .ay(16'd218) .bx(…9'd109…) = 109*C. Soft: p_a9+p_b56. Total 9A+56B+109C.

Every input port is connected by name on all 42 instances; ax operands fit 16 bits (sum_24[16:1] = floor(C/2) < 2^16), the largest bx is 32*(din+n_delay_reg6) < 2^22, and the exact block result stays far below 2^64, so only result[27:0] is ever needed. mult_res is local to each instance and read nowhere else; only dout leaves each module. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true
// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
// reaches result in the same cycle.
module comb_mult_add_16 (
    input  [15:0] ax,
    input  [15:0] ay,
    input  [31:0] bx,
    output [63:0] result
);

    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact

    assign result = sum;

endmodule

PLAN:

This is a revision of the kept candidate (revision 2). It keeps exactly the same block census (42 blocks, one per my_fir instance, 101 DSP tiles) and the same block operands for six of the seven modules; what changes is where the block's result enters the sum and the shape of the soft tree, which is what the measured seed-1 path shows to be costing the period.

Why the kept candidate is 8.16 ns, element by element (from the reported path): reg -> xor LUT (1.229) -> wire into bx (1.209) -> block (2.140) -> adder level (0.888) -> adder level (1.474) -> output LUT + wire (1.126) -> setup. That is pre-block logic of 2.44 ns and two 28-bit adder levels after the block. The rewrite below leaves exactly one adder level between the block and the dout register, and balances the purely-soft side so it arrives no later than the block does. Predicted slowest rewritten stage: soft side ready after 4 levels (0.10 + 4x1.2 = 4.9 ns), block result ready at 4.65-4.68 ns (pair-sum/xor level 1.3 + wire 1.21 + block 2.14), final 28-bit adder 1.2 ns, output LUT + wire + setup 1.13 ns => about 7.2-7.3 ns, against the 8.16 ns the kept candidate leaves. The same model reproduces the kept candidate's measured path to within 0.05 ns (2.54+2.14+1.2+1.2+1.13 = 8.21 vs 8.16 measured), so the 7.2-7.3 ns estimate is on the same footing.

Per-module arithmetic the editor must write (all wires 28 bit; every value below is unsigned and every add/sub is mod 2^28, which is exactly what the original 28-bit dout assignment does, since din and the delay registers are unsigned 16-bit and every coefficient is a positive constant). Write each level as its own named wire so the tree shape survives synthesis; put the assignments outside the always block and leave the always block otherwise untouched (same enable new_data_rdy, same delay-register chain, same output_data_ready).

my_fir_f1 (coefficients 29,101,15,235,15,101,29; A=din+n_delay_reg6, B=n_delay_reg1+n_delay_reg5, C=n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4, D=n_delay_reg3):
block = 235*D + 32*A;
p_b96 = (x_15<<6)+(x_15<<5); p_b5 = (x_15<<2)+x_15; p_c15 = (x_24<<4)-x_24; p_a3 = (x_06<<1)+x_06;
q_b101 = p_b96+p_b5; q_ca = p_c15-p_a3; soft_sum = q_b101+q_ca;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 235D + 32A + 101B + 15C - 3A = 29A+101B+15C+235D, the original sum.

my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (4,42,163,255,163,42,4): block = 326*floor(C/2) + 163*(C mod 2) = 163*C (326*sum_24[16:1] + 163*(n_delay_reg2[0]^n_delay_reg4[0]) is exactly 163*(n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4));
p_b40 = (x_15<<5)+(x_15<<3); p_d255 = (x_3<<8)-x_3; p_a4b2 = (x_06<<2)+(x_15<<1);
q_ab = p_b40+p_a4b2; soft_sum = q_ab+p_d255;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 4A+42B+163C+255D.

my_fir_f3 (12,77,148,0,148,77,12): block = 148*C;
p_a12 = (x_06<<3)+(x_06<<2); p_b72 = (x_15<<6)+(x_15<<3); p_b5 = (x_15<<2)+x_15;
q_b77 = p_b72+p_b5; soft_sum = q_b77+p_a12;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 12A+77B+148C (the original omits the n_delay_reg3 tap, line 1602-1607).

my_fir_h1 (15,25,193,0,193,25,15): block = 193*C;
p_a15 = (x_06<<4)-x_06; p_b24 = (x_15<<4)+(x_15<<3);
q_ab = p_a15+p_b24; soft_sum = q_ab+x_15;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 15A+25B+193C.

my_fir_h3 and my_fir_h4 (9,56,109,0,109,56,9): block = 109*C;
p_a9 = (x_06<<3)+x_06; p_b56 = (x_15<<6)-(x_15<<3); soft_sum = p_a9+p_b56;
dout <= soft_sum + mult_res[27:0]; => 9A+56B+109C.

Correctness. Every my_fir coefficient set is symmetric (c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4), so pairing is exact; sum_24[16:1] is floor((n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4)/2) < 2^16 and fits ax, and the xor term restores the dropped low bit, so the block's unsigned product is the exact pair term. ay constants 235, 326, 296, 386, 218 are all < 2^16; the largest bx is 32*(din+n_delay_reg6) < 2^22, so nothing wraps inside the block's 64-bit result and only result[27:0] is used. All regrouping is addition/subtraction mod 2^28, which matches the original truncation into the 28-bit dout. No design register is moved, removed or added, no reset behaviour changes, and nothing inside a block is read anywhere else: mult_res is local to its instance and only dout leaves the module. No assumption about the design's inputs is needed, so there is no ASSUMES line.

Blocks added and tiles. 42 blocks, one per my_fir instance (7 modules x 6 instances through h_fltr, lines 514-520), each on its own DSP tile; the 294 fltr_compute 9x9 products stay packed four to a tile. Design total 101 DSP tiles (measured census of the kept candidate, which this revision matches exactly), against 224 in the baseline. Block count, tile count and soft-adder count per instance are the same as or one adder below the kept candidate (f1 goes from 9 to 8 28-bit adders, the others are unchanged), so area and wirelength should land on the kept candidate's figures and the gain is the period.

Longest series of blocks in any stage: one. A block never feeds another block; each block's result goes through a single 28-bit adder into the dout register. Block contribution to the stage is 2.14 ns of the ~7.3 ns stage; the rest is 1.3 ns of pair-sum/xor level ahead of it, 1.21 ns of wire into it, 1.2 ns for the one adder after it, and 1.13 ns of output LUT, wire and setup.

What soft logic leaves which stage. The stage affected is the my_fir dout stage, which is the baseline's slowest stage (11.6069 ns, my_fir_f1) and the second slowest (11.293 ns, my_fir_f2), and is still the slowest stage the kept candidate leaves (8.16 ns at seed 1). Out of it go: one hard 18x19 multiply per converted tap and, compared with the kept candidate, one full 28-bit adder level on the block's own path (the block result is now the last term of the sum rather than an input two levels deep). What stays in soft logic is the shift/add tree for the taps the block does not carry, now balanced so that it is ready at the same moment the block result is. Nothing is added to any other stage: the delay-register chain, output_data_ready, and the h_fltr/steer_fltr stages are untouched.

Register stages, before and after, for each converted region. Before: the products are unregistered (the table's "products registered 0 stage(s) before the sum"); operands are din and the delay registers, the seven products and their six-level adder chain are combinational, and the result is captured in dout — one register stage from operands to result. After: identical — one register stage from operands to result. The block is combinational, no design register becomes a block register, no register is moved, and no register is added, so latency and reset behaviour are bit-for-bit unchanged on every cycle.

Candidates left, with reasons.

  • All 42 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071) are left, for three reasons that apply to all of them equally. (i) They already sit four to a DSP tile in mult_9x9_fixed_pt mode on 39 tiles; a block takes a tile alone, so converting even one 8-bit-by-9-bit product would pay a whole tile (253779, about 9 clusters) to save a quarter of one, and converting all of them would cost roughly 250 extra tiles. (ii) Their products are registered one stage before the sum (q1..q7 at line 867 etc.), so a block placed on a product cannot absorb any level of the q -> d_out_tmp adder chain, which is the only part of fltr_compute near the critical path; the stage a block would shorten (din slice -> q) is already short. (iii) Each term enters the 20-bit sum as the sign-extension of a 17-bit truncated product ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q} at line 867), i.e. the term is not the plain unsigned product the block computes; reproducing it needs a per-term 2^17 correction derived from the product's bit 16, which would add logic to the very stage that is already the long one there.
  • Within the converted my_fir modules, the taps not named in REGIONS (my_fir_f1 1486,1487,1488,1490,1491,1492; my_fir_f2 1542,1543,1545,1547,1548; my_fir_f3 1602,1603,1606,1607; my_fir_h1 1661,1662,1665,1666; my_fir_h2 1716,1717,1719,1721,1722; my_fir_h3 1775,1776,1779,1780; my_fir_h4 1833,1834,1837,1838) are not carried by a block: each block has one product port, and these taps are recomputed outside it as the shift/add trees above, which is what makes the regrouping legal. A second block per instance was considered and rejected: it adds 42 tiles and does not shorten the stage, because the pair-sum block's result cannot arrive before about 4.68 ns and the final adder and output LUT after it are unavoidable, so the stage stays at about 7.0-7.2 ns either way.

Risk the plan accepts. The untouched fltr_compute q -> d_out_tmp stage is a chain of six 20-bit adder levels (line 867 and its six siblings); by the same per-level figure it is worth roughly 7.0-7.9 ns, so it may floor the period somewhere in that band and the measured gain may be smaller than the 8.16 -> 7.3 ns the rewritten stage gives. Nothing in this revision makes that stage worse, and area and wirelength are held at the kept candidate's values, so the expected product moves down, not up.

DESIGN_CHANGE: the seven fltr_compute modules sum their seven sign-extended terms as a left-associated chain (line 867 and its siblings at 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073), which synthesises to six adder levels between the q registers and d_out_tmp. Writing that same sum as a balanced tree — the value is identical, since all seven terms are 20-bit values added mod 2^20 — would cut that stage from six levels to three, roughly 3.5 ns, and would remove the floor that now limits what any my_fir rewrite can deliver. It needs no block and is not part of this rewrite, so it is not done here.

Verified against the plan and the rules:

  • Regions/scope. Only the seven my_fir_* modules changed (stereovision2.v:1474-1520, 1558-1600, 1642-1682, 1724-1762, 1800-1842, 1883-1919, 1960-1996). fltr_compute_* is untouched (stereovision2.v:867 still the left-associated chain), matching the plan's decision to leave DESIGN_CHANGE undone. Delay chain, new_data_rdy enable and output_data_ready are unchanged; the only other diff hunks are trailing-whitespace removal on the blank line before output_data_ready.
  • Ports. All 7 instances connect ax, ay, bx and result; ax is 16 bits (n_delay_reg3, or sum_24[16:1] which is 16 bits since sum_24 is 17), ay constants 235/326/296/386/218 all < 2^16, bx concatenations are exactly 32 bits, mult_res is 64 bits. Operands match the plan instance for instance.
  • Arithmetic. With A=din+reg6, B=reg1+reg5, C=reg2+reg4, D=reg3: f1 block = 235D+32A, soft = 101B+15C−3A → 29A+101B+15C+235D (coeffs 29,101,15,235,15,101,29). f2/h2: 326*floor(C/2)+163*(C&1) = 163C since sum_24[0] = reg2[0]^reg4[0]; soft = 4A+42B+255D → 4,42,163,255. f3: 296/148 → 148C, soft 12A+77B (reg3 tap correctly absent, COEF3_d=0). h1: 386/193 → 193C, soft 15A+25B. h3/h4: 218/109 → 109C, soft 9A+56B. All intermediates are 28-bit wires, so every regroup (including the negative q_ca, p_c15, p_d255, p_a15, p_b56 terms) is mod 2^28, exactly what the original truncation into 28-bit dout does; the true sums are ≤ ~4.4e7 < 2^28, so the residue equals the original value. No wrap inside the block (max ax*ay+bx ≈ 2.1e7 ≪ 2^64), so result[27:0] is the exact term.
  • Visibility. mult_res and all new wires are local; only dout/output_data_ready leave each module, and nothing the block consumes is produced solely inside it.
  • Registers/reset. No register added, moved or removed; the block is combinational and sits in the same single register stage from operands to dout, so reset behaviour is unchanged on every cycle. No ASSUMES: needed, consistent with the plan.

1	// comb_mult_add_16: combinational, no clock. result = ax*ay + bx, with ax, ay and bx unsigned
2	// (decision 2026-10-16: every integer mode on this arch is unsigned); the 16x16 product is 32
3	// bits and the sum is formed at 64 bits, so result is exact and never wraps (the 64-bit result
4	// wraps only in principle: no sum of these operands reaches it).
5	// Ports: ax[16], ay[16], bx[32] in; result[64] out. No registers and no reset: every input
6	// reaches result in the same cycle.
7	module comb_mult_add_16 (
8	    input  [15:0] ax,
9	    input  [15:0] ay,
10	    input  [31:0] bx,
11	    output [63:0] result
12	);
13	
14	    wire [31:0] prod = ax * ay;                                      // 16x16 -> 32, exact
15	    wire [63:0] sum  = prod + bx;                                    // zero-extended, exact
16	
17	    assign result = sum;
18	
19	endmodule
20

objective
area x delay x wirelength (delay register to register, 2026-10-20)
baseline
layout koios_small · used area 9.73358e+07 · critical path 11.6069 ns · wirelength 436921 · area x delay x wirelength (delay register to register, 2026-10-20) 4.93619e+14 (read from entry; median per term over the entry's seed runs (its seed_medians; seeds lists them))

The objective is area x delay x wirelength (delay register to register, 2026-10-20): VPR's total used logic block area (I/Os and empty grid tiles excluded) times the critical path times the total routed wirelength. Each term is the median over the loop's seeds; the product is the product of the medians. Beside every product stand the ratios against the baseline, A/A0 (area), D/D0 (critical path), W/W0 (wirelength) and their product, so the normalization can be read off. After each measured rewrite, the planner is given every measurement so far and asked for a revision. A revision is built and checked like the first rewrite, and the lowest product is kept, a later rewrite having to beat it by more than 9.41%. The loop stops when the planner declines to revise, when a revision does not lower the best product by more than 9.41%, when a revision fails its checks, or when 9 revisions have been made.

"Path 1 ends in" is read from the rewrite's own timing report and netlist: the constant coefficients on the block (or plain multiply) that path 1 passes through, matched against the constants each module of the edited RTL multiplies by; two modules that share a coefficient set are both named, and the hover text gives the element and its constants. Verification comes from verification.yaml in the run dir when one was written; the loop itself does not run the equivalence checks. Its label is proven when the LEC closed, simulation under assumption when the simulation passed without a closed proof and the plan stated a bound it rests on, simulation only when it stated none; the hover text gives the simulation and LEC results and the stated bounds.
